implementation.numeric_core_modified_semantics: false means this interface layer (wrapper, pipeline, contract and MCP server) contains no DIC numerics of its own. It is not a claim that the C++/CUDA numerical core is frozen; numerical changes to the core are gated by the production anchors (smoke/run_production_anchors.sh).

pipeline.description: Image sequence to GPU DIC displacement fields (full-field mode, the general entry point) or, when measurement lines are given, to an interface COD CSV (COD mode, laboratory post-processing; COD here is the slip across the interface, outputs.cod_csv).

field_modes.full_field: neither --interface-y nor --line-y: every target frame's full POI grid is written to <output-dir>/<event>/frame_NNNNNN.csv (or .bin with --output-format raw); no aggregation, --cal unused
field_modes.cod: --interface-y or --line-y: the binary computes only the two measurement lines and the pipeline aggregates them into <output-dir>/cod_result.csv (single event) or <output-dir>/<event>.csv (campaign); --cal required

pipeline.validation_scope: --dry-run applies every check: the argument bounds (validate_args), the image-aware line/ROI checks on each event's first frame, duplicate target frame numbers and the state of --output-dir (including whether an existing ledger's target list can be resumed). --strict runs exactly that validation, plus its two strict-only checks (the deprecated lab binary path, a container deeper than 8 bits read as 8-bit), before anything is written and stops with exit 2 when it fails; for a campaign that is all or nothing. Without --strict, normal execution keeps its historical behaviour: the checks it always enforced still stop it with exit 1, and every other argument the dry-run would reject (even --subset, --cal <= 0, --gauge <= 1, L0 == L1, a reversed --roi-cols, ...) is reported as an argument_warning (stderr and summary) while the run proceeds. --events and --event-interface-y are checked the same way in every mode (validate_args lists the campaign directories, no image is read) and refuse with exit 2, without --strict too, before anything is written. After the run every COD result is checked (cod_empty, cod_line_missing, cod_all_zero). MCP plans and runs always pass --strict, after the MCP server's own parameter checks.

parameters.name: --photo-dir
parameters.semantics: Campaign root; each child directory with recognized images is one event.

parameters.name: --image-dir
parameters.semantics: Single-event image directory; first sorted frame is the fixed reference.

parameters.name: --output-dir
parameters.semantics: Pipeline output root. Normal execution creates it (mkdir -p) and also accepts an existing one. --dry-run does not create it but reports its state (outputs.dry_run output_state): an existing file at this path or an unwritable location is an error, an earlier COD CSV that would be replaced is a cod_csv_exists warning, an earlier frame ledger is a frame_dir_has_ledger warning (the binary resumes it only when binary, inputs, parameters and target prefix are unchanged, otherwise it rejects the run), and frames without a ledger are a frame_dir_untracked error. Use a new directory per run.

parameters.name: --interface-y
parameters.semantics: Interface center y (reference-image row, increasing downward). Optional: supplying it (or --line-y) selects COD mode; with neither the pipeline runs the general full-field mode. The lines are L0 = interface_y - gauge//2 and L1 = interface_y + gauge//2. Ignored when --line-y is also supplied. In a campaign it is the default row and --event-interface-y overrides it for matching events.

parameters.name: --line-y
parameters.semantics: Two explicit measurement-line y coordinates; selects COD mode and overrides --interface-y and --gauge. The fill-boundary extrapolation target is the midpoint (L0+L1)/2, not any --interface-y also given. The order sets the COD sign (COD = L0 side minus L1 side); the pipeline does not require L0 < L1.

parameters.name: --events
parameters.semantics: Campaign only (--photo-dir): process only some events. A comma-separated list of event names and glob patterns (fnmatch, case-sensitive; no commas inside a pattern), for example 'event0*,event1*,event20' or 'event2[1-5]'. An event is selected when any item matches its directory name. Every item must match at least one event (a subdirectory with recognized images): a name that is not an event is event_not_found, a pattern that matches nothing is event_pattern_no_match, an empty selection is no_events_selected, an empty item is invalid_events and --image-dir is events_requires_photo_dir. These are checked before any image is read and stop the run with exit 2 in every mode (with or without --strict; the dry-run reports them as errors); nothing is written except a failure summary at --json-summary when one was given. The selection, the number of events left out and their names are in event_selection of the dry-run and the summary; the left-out events are not planned, run or reported (event_without_images too). null: every event, as before 2026-10-05.

parameters.name: --event-interface-y
parameters.semantics: Campaign only: per-event interface rows. Repeatable PATTERN=Y (PATTERN an event name or fnmatch glob, case-sensitive, one per option; Y an integer row >= 0): the selected events whose name matches PATTERN use interface row Y, every other event uses --interface-y, which is required. The lines are Y - gauge//2 and Y + gauge//2 with the run-wide --gauge. Errors (exit 2 in every mode, before any image is read): invalid_event_interface_y (not PATTERN=Y, Y not an integer or negative, commas in PATTERN), event_interface_y_requires_photo_dir, event_interface_y_requires_interface_y, event_interface_y_with_line_y (--line-y fixes both lines for every event), event_interface_y_no_match (an option that applies to no selected event, including one that matches only events --events leaves out) and event_interface_y_conflict (one event matched by options with different rows; options that agree are allowed). Each event's row, its source (interface_y or event_interface_y) and the matching options are events[].geometry interface_y, interface_y_source and interface_y_overrides in the dry-run and the summary; event_selection lists every option with the events it applies to. The image-aware bounds (interface_y_out_of_bounds, line_y_out_of_bounds, line_y_inside_binary_margin) are checked per event with that event's row. null: one row for every event, as before 2026-10-05. MCP does not take it.

parameters.name: --cal
parameters.semantics: Spatial calibration used for x_mm and cod_um. Required in COD mode and unused in full-field mode, where its value is not checked at all (as in 638ad18). In COD mode NaN and Infinity stop the run with an argument error (exit 2; the dry-run reports invalid_cal); a finite value <= 0 is a dry-run error and, without --strict, an argument_warning (a negative value flips the sign of cod_um and x_mm). Use 1.0 only for explicitly uncalibrated pixel-relative work; then x_mm is in pixels and cod_um / 1000 is in pixels.

parameters.name: --subset
parameters.semantics: SUBSET SIZE, not radius. Pipeline conversion is radius=(size-1)//2; --subset 15 means binary radius 7. An even or out-of-range size is a dry-run error and, without --strict, an argument_warning: --subset 16 runs as radius 7, exactly like 15.

parameters.name: --step
parameters.semantics: POI grid spacing forwarded as binary grid_space.

parameters.name: --output-format
parameters.semantics: Frame payload format in full-field mode. COD mode reads frame CSV and rejects raw.

parameters.name: --image-pattern
parameters.semantics: Image-discovery regex searched against each file name, case-insensitive. Default is the historical six-trailing-digits rule. A first capture group of digits becomes the frame number; otherwise frames are numbered from 1 in sort order.

parameters.name: --image-order
parameters.semantics: Sequence ordering strategy. frame-number keeps the historical behaviour; name sorts by file name.

parameters.name: --max-frames
parameters.semantics: Process only the first N target frames after the reference (in the same sort order), for a quick trial run; null means all. The dry-run plans the same N (events[].target_frames, with target_frames_available for the full count), the summary records target_frames_available / target_frames_selected and an info max_frames_applied warning. The truncated target list is a prefix of the full one, so the binary can later extend the same frame directory to more frames (append). MCP plan and run tools take it as max_frames.

parameters.name: --roi-cols
parameters.semantics: Inclusive horizontal filter for final COD aggregation; it does not reduce binary frame-field POIs.

parameters.name: --gauge
parameters.semantics: Requested separation when --interface-y is active; implementation uses half=gauge//2, so actual line separation is 2*(gauge//2) (default 35 produces 34 px). Ignored by --line-y. --gauge <= 0 (invalid_gauge) and --gauge 1 (both lines on one row, line_y_not_distinct, all-zero COD) are dry-run errors and, without --strict, argument_warning entries.

parameters.name: --cod-method
parameters.semantics: naive (the default since 2026-10-05, and before 2026-07-09) is u_L0-u_L1 without extrapolation; fillboundary (optional; the default from 2026-07-09 to 2026-10-05) extrapolates each line's u along its uy to the midpoint row (L0+L1)/2 before differencing. Single-point fillboundary values are noisier and more sensitive to a misplaced interface row (pitfall cod-method-generation).

parameters.name: --conv-threshold
parameters.semantics: Always forwarded explicitly to pin CPU-aligned ICGN convergence semantics. NaN and Infinity are rejected by the argument parser (exit 2).

parameters.name: --input-depth
parameters.semantics: Null means do not forward and retain binary legacy 8-bit default. Left-shifted 12-bit data (uint16 container, low 4 bits always zero, max > 4095) requires explicit 12; auto reads it as 16.

parameters.name: --input-align
parameters.semantics: 12-bit storage alignment. Only legal with --input-depth 12; left-shifted 12-bit data requires left.

parameters.name: --input-normalize
parameters.semantics: Optional linear grayscale scaling; ZNCC displacement is invariant to this scaling.

parameters.name: --gpu-device
parameters.semantics: CUDA device index.

parameters.name: --gpu-bin
parameters.semantics: GPU CLI path. Unset resolves through $FASTICGN_GPU_BIN, then the optional config file [paths].gpu_bin, then the repository build/ trees, then the deprecated lab path (which emits a path_resolution warning; --strict refuses it with gpu_bin_legacy_lab_path). Whatever the source, a relative path is made absolute by prepending the current directory (nothing else: '..' after a symlinked directory still follows the symlink), so dry-run and run use the same file. When the binary did not come from this option or this checkout's build/ trees, the dry-run, the console banner and the summary carry an info-level gpu_bin_outside_checkout note (normal for a lab deployment configured through the config file). MCP fixes this to the operator-configured binary rather than accepting arbitrary executables.

parameters.name: --keep-frames
parameters.semantics: Retain intermediate 9-column frame CSV files after COD aggregation. Full-field mode always keeps its frame payloads, which are the product. Frames are kept when the binary or the aggregation fails. After an empty COD result (cod_empty) they are deleted like after any other aggregation, as in 638ad18, because a kept frame directory carries the binary's ledger and a rerun with corrected parameters into the same --output-dir would then be rejected (resume rejected); --keep-frames, or --strict, keeps them in place.

parameters.name: --strict
parameters.semantics: Opt-in hard mode. Before anything is written, run the complete --dry-run validation (argument bounds, image-aware checks, duplicate target frame numbers, output directory state, and two checks only --strict makes: the deprecated lab binary path, and a first frame in a container deeper than 8 bits that would be read as 8-bit, input_depth_truncates_container, whose message names the probe's recommended --input-depth/--input-align) and stop with exit 2 and a pipeline_error summary when it fails. The pre-check is all or nothing: one refused event of a campaign stops the whole campaign before any event runs. Its warnings and notes are written to the summary's top-level warning_details (stage strict_precheck; warn-level ones also to the top-level warnings). After the run, cod_all_zero and duplicate_frame_number count as failures of their event, the frames of an empty COD stay in place for diagnosis, and any failed event makes the process exit 3. Without it the historical exit codes are kept: a failed single event exits 1 and a campaign exits 0 whatever its events did. MCP plans and runs always pass it (mcp.run_params.strict).

parameters.name: --saturation-warn-fraction
parameters.unit: fraction of reference-frame pixels (COD mode: of a measurement-line band)
parameters.semantics: Heuristic, tunable threshold for input_8bit_max_255: when the reference frame (read at effective depth 8) has a pixel at 255, the warning is info if the graded fraction of pixels at 255 is at most this value and warn above it (always warn when the file's container is deeper than 8 bits, which hints at high-bit truncation). What is graded depends on the mode. COD mode: each measurement line's band, the pixels of that line's subsets that enter the COD aggregation (rows L - r .. L + r; columns x0 - r .. x1 + r for --roi-cols x0,x1, otherwise the binary's first and last POI column on the line +/- r; clipped to the image), and the largest band fraction decides. Full-field mode: the whole reference frame. The default 0.05 (0.02 for the whole frame until 2026-10-04) is a heuristic, not a limit calibrated against correlation error: the whole-frame fraction of lab frames is dominated by fixed bright pixels outside the measurement bands (docs/quality-checks.md section 5). The graded value, the threshold and the per-line numbers are in events[].input_saturation (also in the dry-run).

parameters.name: --json-summary
parameters.semantics: Atomically write schema_version=1 run summary. Ignored in dry-run, whose JSON is stdout. If writing it fails, a minimal failure summary (pipeline_error: summary_write_failed) is attempted in its place and the process exits 1. It also changes campaign control flow: with it, an event directory holding a single image is reported as a failed event and an exception inside one event is recorded and the campaign continues; without it, single-image event directories are skipped silently and an exception aborts the whole campaign.

parameters.name: --dry-run
parameters.semantics: Read-only validation and complete command planning; stdout JSON, no output directory, no GPU process. Recognised in any unambiguous abbreviation (--dry), so that even a parse error comes back as JSON.

parameters.name: --describe
parameters.semantics: Print this contract byte-for-byte to stdout and exit without requiring normal arguments; any unambiguous abbreviation (--desc) works, and any other argument next to it is an error (exit 2).

binary.name: opencorr_cli_cuda_mvp
binary.subset_semantics: POSITIONAL subset_radius is RADIUS, not size. This differs from pipeline --subset.

positionals.name: subset_radius
positionals.semantics: subset RADIUS, not full size; replaced by --subset-size N when that option is given

positionals.name: output_path
positionals.semantics: CSV output path or raw-output base path

positionals.name: subset_radius
positionals.semantics: subset RADIUS, not full size; replaced by --subset-size N when that option is given

version.stdout_semantics: a title line, then one key=value line per field in this order; nothing on stderr, no status line. name, git_hash and build_date are the stable first lines. version is the semantic version (the CMake project version, with -dev between releases; CITATION.cff carries it with a leading v). git_dirty is 1 when tracked files differed from git_hash at build time, 0 when they did not, unknown outside a git checkout (git_hash is then unknown too). backend is cuda or cpu; fftw is 1 when the FFTW CPU FFTCC is built in. git_hash and git_dirty are sampled on every build, build_date when the build tree was configured. Binaries built before 2026-10-05 print only the first three fields

help.selector: --help or -h anywhere on the command line, except as the value of an option that takes one (--output-dir -h names a directory) and after --verify-only, whose argument is always a directory
help.semantics: prints the usage text and then every option with its default on stdout and exits 0; nothing on stderr, no status line. Usage errors keep printing 'Error: ...' and the usage text (without the defaults table) on stderr and exit 1
help.availability: binaries whose --version prints a version= line (built from 2026-10-05 on); earlier ones answer 'Error: unknown option: --help' and exit 1

verify_only.semantics: read-only audit of one multi-frame output directory. It computes nothing, opens no GPU and creates, moves, repairs or rewrites nothing (no quarantine, no archiving of leftovers). It reads the contract, checks every promised payload against its ledger record (size and XXH3-128 digest), the completion record against the contract, each manifest against the completion record and, for raw output, against the contract's frame list, lists leftovers of interrupted runs and entries the ledger does not name, and compares every input image with the fingerprint in the contract
verify_only.stdout: one JSON object on one line (schema fasticgn.verify-only/1); a one-line summary and each problem also go to stderr

status_values.complete: every promised file is present and matches its ledger record, complete.json belongs to this contract and the manifests match it. Exit 0. inputs.status may still be missing (the images are no longer at the recorded paths and were not compared)
status_values.incomplete: nothing contradicts the ledger, but the run is not finished: payloads or a manifest are missing, complete.json is absent or belongs to another target list, or an append was cut off right after its first new output (appended_published is then not empty). Rerunning the interrupted command resumes it; for an append that is the command with the longer target list, unchanged and without --repair (the shorter list is no longer accepted)
status_values.damaged: something contradicts the ledger: a payload whose size or digest differs, a payload or a ledger record without its counterpart, a manifest that does not parse or no longer matches the completion record or the frame list, a damaged contract or completion record, or an entry of any type (file, symlink, directory) that carries the extension of the run's outputs in that directory and is not in the ledger. Rerunning the interrupted command with --repair regenerates tracked files; untracked_outputs have to be moved away by hand
status_values.inputs_changed: the outputs are complete and match the ledger, but an input image no longer has the recorded content: the frames describe images that are no longer at those paths
status_values.locked: another process holds the directory lock (a run is in progress); verify again when it has finished
status_values.not_a_run: no .opencorr-state/contract.json: not a ledgered multi-frame output directory (single-frame output and binaries older than the ledger write none), or not a directory
status_values.error: the directory could not be read (an I/O error, named in problems), or the command line did not name exactly one non-empty directory (output_dir is then null)

verify_only.field_semantics: complete is true only for status complete, and exit_code is then 0, otherwise 1. frames_* count frame payloads, files_* also diagnostics files and manifests. missing, mismatched, no_intent, invalid_intent, untracked_outputs, untracked and residue each list at most 20 names, with the exact total in <name>_count. appended_published is listed and counted the same way. untracked_outputs holds unledgered entries with the extension of the outputs published in that directory (.bin or .csv next to the frames, .csv in the diagnostics directory), whatever their file type. untracked holds every other entry the ledger does not name; the run's own --tar-list file is usually one of them (the pipeline keeps tar_list.txt there), so it is information, not a problem, although a rerun of the original command rejects any such entry other than its --tar-list file: complete describes the outputs, it does not promise that a rerun is accepted. residue (temporary files) is a leftover of an interrupted run, archived by the next run. pending_append says whether contract.pending.json exists and pending_append_state what it is: none; append (it extends the recorded contract: an append that has not been promoted); promoted (it repeats the recorded contract, a leftover); unrelated or unreadable (ignored). In state append, appended_published names the appended outputs already on disk that the longer list would accept (promised by the pending contract, regular file, size and digest equal to their own ledger record); appended outputs on disk that fail this are filed under mismatched, no_intent or invalid_intent. inputs is {status: match | changed | missing, checked, changed, missing}. contract summarises the recorded run: digest, schema_version, git_hash, build_date, binary_digest, reference, options, and legacy_scheduling_options (which of gpu_device, threads, preload, decode_threads an older binary still recorded). tool, version and git_hash name the binary that did the checking
verify_only.exit_codes: 0 only for status complete; 1 for every other status, including a missing, empty or extra argument (status error on stdout, an Error line on stderr)
verify_only.lock: a shared lock on the directory is held while reading, so several audits can run together; a run started during an audit is refused with 'run directory already locked' and can simply be started again
verify_only.scope: the directory may have been written by another binary: the audit needs no matching executable. It does not judge measurement quality (see docs/quality-checks.md) and cannot verify a directory without its .opencorr-state
verify_only.availability: binaries whose --version prints a version= line (built from 2026-10-05 on); earlier ones report an unknown option

parameters.name: --gpu-device
parameters.semantics: CUDA device for FFTCC, and for ICGN unless --dual-gpu is given (which runs ICGN on devices 0 and 1 whatever this value is); validated only when CUDA initializes. Scheduling only: the output bytes do not depend on it and it is not part of the resume contract (see binary.resume_contract)

parameters.name: --subset-size
parameters.semantics: subset full SIZE alias for the positional subset_radius; radius = (size - 1) / 2, so --subset-size 15 equals radius 7. Supplying both is rejected; output is byte-identical either way

parameters.name: --max-iter
parameters.semantics: maximum ICGN iterations per POI

parameters.name: --conv-threshold
parameters.semantics: ICGN convergence threshold; 0.001 matches the CPU reference

parameters.name: --threads
parameters.semantics: OpenMP host-side thread count. Scheduling only: the output bytes do not depend on it and it is not part of the resume contract (see binary.resume_contract)

parameters.name: --line
parameters.semantics: values append across repeated flags; non-negative y inside binary subset margin are used, margin violations warn and skip

parameters.name: --dual-gpu
parameters.semantics: split the ICGN POIs across CUDA devices 0 and 1; FFTCC stays on --gpu-device

parameters.name: --durability
parameters.semantics: publication durability policy. rename publishes every file through a private temporary plus atomic rename/link with zero fsync per frame and takes one constant barrier over ledger and manifests when a multi-frame job completes; fsync additionally forces every payload, ledger record and directory to the device (about 4 fsync per frame). Both are crash-consistent; neither changes output bytes and neither enters the resume contract

parameters.name: --repair
parameters.semantics: on resume, move damaged tracked frames (truncated, same-size corruption, missing or invalid intent, unparsable manifest, damaged completion/manifest records) into .opencorr-state/quarantine/<timestamp>/ and regenerate them by replay. Crash temporaries are archived on every resume, with or without this flag. I/O faults (a metadata file that is missing, unopenable or unreadable) are reported with their errno and exit 1 instead of being repaired. Changed inputs/parameters/binary, reordered or shortened target lists, unknown files and output symlinks stay rejected

parameters.name: --no-repair
parameters.semantics: explicitly keep the default hard rejection of damaged tracked frames

parameters.name: --quiet
parameters.semantics: drop the per-frame progress lines from stderr (the [n/N] line and the [BASELINE], [FALLBACK] and [POI-FALLBACK] lines); the run header, warnings, errors, the closing totals and the stdout status line stay. Presentation only: it changes no output byte and is not part of the resume contract. No effect in single-frame mode, which prints no per-frame lines. Without it stderr is unchanged. Available in binaries whose --version prints a version= line (built from 2026-10-05 on)

parameters.name: --skip-fftcc
parameters.semantics: reuse previous-frame displacement seeds and skip FFTCC after the first target when quality permits

parameters.name: --no-skip-fftcc
parameters.semantics: force FFTCC initialization on every target frame

parameters.name: --poi-fallback
parameters.semantics: repair bad POIs only on the multi-frame skip-FFTCC path; accepted but has no effect in single-frame mode

parameters.name: --no-poi-fallback
parameters.semantics: disable POI-level repair on the multi-frame skip-FFTCC path

parameters.name: --temporal-extrapolation
parameters.semantics: opt in to two-frame temporal displacement extrapolation; single-frame parsing accepts it but no temporal history exists

parameters.name: --no-temporal-extrapolation
parameters.semantics: explicitly retain previous-frame (zero-order) temporal seeds

parameters.name: --output-format
parameters.semantics: select CSV or 36-byte raw records; binary is accepted as an alias for raw

parameters.name: --kernel
parameters.semantics: select the ICGN iteration kernel: warp-per-POI (default since 2026-09-02) or legacy block-per-POI (pre-2026-09 production baseline, kept as byte-identical A/B reference)

parameters.name: --fftcc
parameters.semantics: select the FFTCC initial-guess backend: gpu = batched cuFFT (default in CUDA builds, no FFTW linkage), cpu = legacy FFTW path (requires an OPENCORR_GPU_MVP_WITH_FFTW=ON build; non-CUDA builds default to cpu)

parameters.name: --input-depth
parameters.semantics: select legacy 8-bit loading, explicit high-bit loading, or runtime inference

parameters.name: --input-align
parameters.constraint: right/left are legal only when input-depth=12; default auto is legal for other depths
parameters.semantics: interpret 12-bit values inside a uint16 container; left divides stored values by 16

parameters.name: --input-normalize
parameters.semantics: apply optional linear grayscale scaling before correlation

parameters.name: --diagnostics
parameters.semantics: write per-frame iteration/convergence/status diagnostics through a bounded background writer; publication failures fail the job

parameters.name: --diagnostics-dir
parameters.semantics: empty internal default while diagnostics is disabled; a supplied path also enables diagnostics

parameters.name: --binary-output
parameters.semantics: legacy flag selecting raw binary output

parameters.name: --preload
parameters.semantics: preload target images on a host worker during multi-frame execution. Scheduling only, not part of the resume contract

parameters.name: --no-preload
parameters.semantics: load target images synchronously in the multi-frame loop. Scheduling only, not part of the resume contract

parameters.name: --decode-threads
parameters.semantics: image decode worker count for the multi-frame preloader; up to N frames are in flight, delivered in frame order, and decoded bytes are identical for any count. Scheduling only, not part of the resume contract

parameters.name: --output-roi
parameters.semantics: write-side output crop: keep only POIs whose integer coordinates fall in the inclusive rectangle; compute and QA still cover the full field; recorded in the raw manifest

parameters.name: --output-step
parameters.semantics: write-side output subsampling: keep only POIs whose x and y are both multiples of N. This is not every N-th grid point (the usage text of binaries built before 2026-10-05 says it is): the grid starts at margin = radius + 2, so for example radius 7 with grid spacing 2 and --output-step 2 keeps no POI at all, writes empty frames and still exits 0. Compute and QA still cover the full field; recorded in the raw manifest

process_output.stdout: every computing invocation (single-frame and multi-frame, successful or not, including a command line that was rejected) ends with exactly one JSON line, the status line. --version, --help and --verify-only print their own answer instead and no status line. A process that is killed or crashes prints none, so a missing status line means the run did not end by itself. The line is written even when the reader has closed the pipe (no SIGPIPE death). One exception: when stdout is non-blocking and has no room (a full pipe whose reader is busy) the binary waits up to 5 s in total for room; if the reader makes none, the line is missing or cut short although the run ended by itself with its normal exit code
process_output.status_line_semantics: status is ok exactly when exit_code is 0, otherwise error. error is the text of the first 'Error:' line (null on success). mode is single-frame, multi-frame, or null when the command line was rejected before a mode was chosen. frames_total counts the targets requested; frames_processed those computed by this invocation (a resume replays from frame 1, so it counts every frame again); frames_skipped those left alone because the directory verified as a complete run (frames_processed is then 0). output_dir is absolute; output_path exists only in single-frame mode; output_format is csv or raw. The line is strict UTF-8: single-frame mode accepts an output path that is not valid UTF-8 and writes the file there, but output_dir and output_path then show each undecodable byte as U+FFFD and no longer locate the file (multi-frame mode rejects such paths at startup). elapsed_sec is the wall time of the whole process. git_dirty is true, false or null. totals (multi-frame runs that computed and succeeded) holds skip_fftcc_frames, fallback_frames, poi_fallback_frames, poi_fallback_pois, poi_fallback_recovered, temporal_seed_frames, temporal_seed_pois and resumed_from_existing_files. warnings holds the text of the first 20 'Warning:' lines, warning_count their total
process_output.stderr: the run header, one progress line per frame plus [BASELINE], [FALLBACK] and [POI-FALLBACK] lines, warnings, errors and the closing totals. --quiet drops only the per-frame lines. The pipeline keeps the whole stream as events[].binary_stderr_log and discards the binary's stdout
process_output.availability: binaries whose --version prints a version= line (built from 2026-10-05 on); earlier ones print nothing on stdout except for --version
process_output.audit_basis: Contract auditing used printUsage, parseCommonOption, --help and --version.

resume_contract.compared_on_resume: the executable's content fingerprint, git_hash and build_date; the reference image's canonical path and content fingerprint; options radius, step, dual_gpu, kernel, fftcc, max_iteration, convergence, skip_fftcc, poi_fallback, temporal_extrapolation, format, line_ys, input_depth, input_align, input_normalize, output_roi_enabled, output_roi, output_step, diagnostics, diagnostics_dir; and the target list (each input's path and fingerprint, output_name and file), which may only grow by appending
resume_contract.not_compared: --durability, --repair, --quiet, and the scheduling options --gpu-device, --threads, --preload / --no-preload and --decode-threads. On 2026-10-05 each scheduling option was varied against the 60-frame production anchor (11 combinations, both GPUs) and against the CPU-only and the --fftcc cpu backends: every output tree was byte-identical. The manifest's engine block still records the values of the run that wrote it
resume_contract.legacy: binaries whose --version prints no version= line wrote the four scheduling options into the contract and compare them, so with those binaries a different --threads (including the default, which follows the CPUs the process may use), --gpu-device, --preload or --decode-threads rejects the resume. Newer binaries ignore the four keys in such a contract
resume_contract.rejection_message: 'resume rejected: run configuration/reference/binary changed (recorded -> requested): <field>: <old> -> <new>; ...' names every differing contract field with both values (options.max_iteration: 10 -> 11, binary.digest, reference.content.digest, ...) and says which kind of change it is; 'resume rejected: targets changed/reordered; ...' names the first differing target or the two list lengths. Binaries whose --version prints no version= line print only the first sentence
resume_contract.other_binaries: the executable's fingerprint is part of the contract, so a directory can only be resumed by the byte-identical binary that wrote it, never by an older or newer build (rebuilding the same commit also changes it). Any ledger-aware binary rejects a foreign directory and leaves it untouched; binaries older than the ledger (2026-09-17) do not see it: they skip the frames that exist and compute the rest from a new baseline, which gives different numbers, so never point them at an existing directory. --verify-only needs no matching binary

frame_csv.availability: COD mode: intermediate files in <output-dir>/_frames_<event>/, deleted after a successful aggregation unless --keep-frames. Full-field mode: the product, always kept in <output-dir>/<event>/ (with --output-format raw they are .bin files described by raw_manifest instead).
frame_csv.file_naming: frame_NNNNNN.csv where NNNNNN is the zero-padded frame number the pipeline assigned to the target image (see cod_csv frame); the reference image has no file

columns.name: x
columns.meaning: POI center x: reference-image column, increasing to the right

columns.name: y
columns.meaning: POI center y: reference-image row, increasing downward

columns.name: u
columns.meaning: x displacement from the reference image (+x right)

columns.name: v
columns.meaning: y displacement from the reference image (+y down)

columns.name: zncc
columns.meaning: quality/status; zncc<0 is not a valid displacement row

frame_csv.serialization: x/y are integers; floating columns use general format with six significant digits
frame_csv.validity_rule: For binary-compatible valid_ratio use finite(zncc) && zncc>=0. For displacement statistics additionally require finite(u) && finite(v).
frame_csv.status_rule: zncc<0 carries boundary/failure/status rows; u and v may be seeds or failed-iteration residue and must be filtered.

columns.name: frame
columns.meaning: frame number of the target image as the pipeline assigned it: the first capture group of --image-pattern when it is all digits (by default the six digits before the extension), otherwise the 1-based position in sort order. It is the NNNNNN of _frames_<event>/frame_NNNNNN.csv. The reference image (the first in sort order) has no rows.

columns.name: x_mm
columns.meaning: x_px * cal, where x_px is the POI column in reference-image pixels. The origin is image column 0, not the --roi-cols start. Only POI columns inside --roi-cols (inclusive) appear; the column set is taken from the first frame CSV.

columns.name: cod_um
columns.unit: micrometre when cal is in mm/px
columns.meaning: slip across the interface: the relative displacement of its two sides, i.e. the difference of the horizontal displacement u between the two lines, L0 side minus L1 side. It is not an opening displacement; the names cod_um, --cod-method and COD are historical and are kept. naive (default since 2026-10-05): 1000 * cal * (u_L0 - u_L1); fillboundary (--cod-method fillboundary; the default from 2026-07-09 to 2026-10-05): 1000 * cal * ([u_L0 + uy_L0 * (y0 - L0)] - [u_L1 + uy_L1 * (y0 - L1)]) with y0 = (L0 + L1) / 2, i.e. each line's u is extrapolated along its own uy = du/dy to the midpoint between the lines. L0 is the first --line-y value or interface_y - gauge//2, L1 the second or interface_y + gauge//2. The sign is fixed by that order and by nothing else (positive when the, possibly extrapolated, u on the L0 side exceeds the one on the L1 side, for cal > 0); the pipeline does not require L0 < L1, and reversing the order flips every sign. The method actually used is events[].cod_mode in the summary.

cod_csv.point_rule: a (frame, x) point is written only when both lines have a valid row there (finite zncc >= 0) and the result is finite; otherwise it is omitted
cod_csv.serialization: x_mm and cod_um use four digits after the decimal point; non-finite COD points are omitted rather than written as NaN; rows are grouped by ascending frame, x ascending within a frame; the reference frame has no row
cod_csv.row_count_expectation: at most events[].frames x the number of POI columns inside --roi-cols; fewer rows mean points were omitted. The summary checks this for you in events[].cod_stats: a header-only file is cod_empty (event status fail, and cod_line_missing when a line had no row at all), a file whose cod_um values are all 0.0000 is cod_all_zero (warn; fail with --strict), and target frames without any point are cod_frames_without_points (warn).
cod_csv.publication: written to a temporary file in the same directory and renamed over the target, so the target is either the previous file or the complete new one

ordinary_csv_manifest.note: The pipeline uses binary CSV mode, which writes no binary manifest. Pipeline provenance comes from binary --version.

raw_manifest.file_naming: multi-frame: manifest.opencorr-raw.json in the output directory; single-frame: the .bin output path plus .manifest.json (out.csv becomes out.bin and out.bin.manifest.json)
raw_manifest.output_filter_semantics: present only when --output-roi or --output-step is active; roi is present only when roi_enabled is true
raw_manifest.engine_semantics: what actually ran, for replay and audit: solver backend and iteration kernel, out-of-bounds policy, FFTCC backend, the skip/fallback/temporal seeding policies, durability, build identity (version and git_dirty, true / false / null, since 2026-10-05: null means not built from a git checkout), host thread counts and the CUDA device. threads, decode_threads, preload and gpu_device are those of the run that wrote the manifest; they do not affect the output and a resume may use others. cuda is null in CPU-only builds, and each of its members is null when the CUDA query failed. Additive metadata only: frame payload bytes are unchanged, and the run ledger digests whatever manifest it finds, so completion records stay consistent. Manifests written before 2026-09-17 have no engine block.
raw_manifest.oob_policy_semantics: geometric-v1: a POI whose warped target subset has any sample outside the bicubic interpolatable range is rejected with zncc = -3 (docs/output-format.md). Absent from manifests written before 2026-09-17, which predate the rule.
raw_manifest.frame_fallback_policy_semantics: how the skip-FFTCC whole-frame fallback (skip attempt bad fraction above the first target's bad_ratio + 0.03; bad = non-finite zncc or zncc < 0.8, -3 not counted) combines its from-scratch pass (FFTCC from a zero guess, then ICGN) with the skip attempt. per-poi-merge-v1: a good skip result (finite zncc >= 0.8) is kept; a bad one is replaced only when the from-scratch zncc is finite, not -3 and at least as high (the POI-level repair rule); a -3 one only by a good from-scratch result, unlike the POI-level repair where -3 is terminal. The merged frame never has more bad POIs than the skip attempt; frame bad_ratio is the merged value. Once triggered the fallback may fire on every later frame, each time adding a full-frame FFTCC + ICGN. Absent from manifests of earlier builds, whose fallback replaced the whole skip attempt.
raw_manifest.durability_semantics: effective --durability policy of the run that wrote the manifest; informational, it never changes frame payload bytes
raw_manifest.input_image_semantics: depth, align, normalize and imread_flags are the requested options, not per-frame auto effective values. With the default depth 8 the image is read with IMREAD_GRAYSCALE, which reduces a 16-bit file to 8 bits before the solver sees it. reference_source_depth is the OpenCV depth of the reference file as stored (CV_8U, CV_16U, ...), read once more with IMREAD_ANYDEPTH when depth is 8, so a 16-bit source stays visible; reference_source_range is its [min, max] stored value; both are null when that read failed. target_source_depth_mismatches counts the target frames whose stored depth differs from the reference: with depth 8 the file headers are compared (TIFF, PNG, JPEG, PNM and BMP), otherwise the decoded depths. Stored depths up to 8 bits count as one grey scale (OpenCV expands them all to full-range 8-bit samples); above 8 bits the depths must be equal. A frame whose header cannot be read is not compared and not counted: another container, a Netpbm header that does not end within the first 512 bytes, a TIFF BitsPerSample that is neither SHORT nor LONG, a truncated file. The three fields are information, not part of the resume contract, and exist in manifests written by binaries whose --version prints a version= line (built from 2026-10-05 on). Those binaries also warn (stderr and status line) when a reference deeper than 8 bits is read with depth 8 and when a target differs from the reference.
raw_manifest.frame_qa_semantics: bad_ratio: fraction of all POIs whose zncc is non-finite or below 0.8, not counting zncc = -3, measured after any fallback. baseline_bad_ratio: set once, from the first target frame. fallback_threshold = baseline_bad_ratio + 0.03. fallback_used: the seeded attempt's bad ratio (printed on the [FALLBACK] stderr line, not stored) exceeded the threshold, so the whole frame was recomputed from a zero initial guess (FFTCC + ICGN) and merged with the seeded attempt per POI as engine.frame_fallback_policy describes; bad_ratio is then the merged value and never exceeds the seeded attempt's. Manifests without frame_fallback_policy come from builds whose fallback replaced the seeded attempt unconditionally. skip_fftcc_used: the frame was attempted with previous-frame seeds instead of FFTCC. poi_fallback_count / poi_fallback_recovered: POIs submitted to / recovered by the per-POI fallback. valid_ratio: fraction with finite zncc >= 0. CSV runs write no manifest; the same per-frame numbers then appear only on the binary's stderr ([FALLBACK] / [POI-FALLBACK] lines and the closing 'Frames with fallback FFTCC' totals), which the pipeline does not keep.

diagnostics_manifest.engine_semantics: identical engine block to the raw manifest
diagnostics_manifest.status_rule: finite zncc>=0 maps to 1; negative zncc is preserved; non-finite zncc maps to -5
diagnostics_manifest.provenance_limitation: the engine block records build identity (git_hash, build_date), kernel, policies and device, but the manifest does not record the subset radius, grid spacing, convergence threshold or input options; those are in the run ledger (.opencorr-state/contract.json) and, for raw runs, in the raw manifest
diagnostics_manifest.output_filter_note: --output-roi and --output-step do not apply to diagnostics CSV files, which always cover the full field, and this manifest carries no output_filter block

run_state.path: .opencorr-state/ inside every multi-frame binary --output-dir (for the pipeline: <output-dir>/_frames_<event>/ in COD mode, <output-dir>/<event>/ in full-field mode); a separate --diagnostics-dir shares this ledger
run_state.availability: multi-frame runs in both CSV and raw format; single-frame mode has no ledger
run_state.purpose: integrity and resume ledger: run contract (binary/input/parameter identity), one per-file commit intent, the completion record and any quarantined files
run_state.archival_rule: copy or move it together with the frame files; without it the frames are untracked and a later run in the same directory is rejected
run_state.visibility: hidden dot-directory; pipeline and MCP frame_*.csv / *.json globs do not match it
run_state.safe_to_delete: only when the frames are final and no resume is wanted; deleting it makes the directory unusable for resume
run_state.completion_semantics: complete.json records that a run once completed. A later run that starts changing the directory (resume, append, repair) does not invalidate it first, so after a crash it can still be present while frames are missing or the manifest is older. To ask whether a directory is complete without changing it, use the binary's --verify-only (binary.modes.verify_only): it computes and writes nothing and needs neither the original command nor the same binary. Rerunning the identical command is the other check: a complete, matching run prints 'Verified complete run' and rewrites nothing, but an incomplete one resumes and computes, and it needs the same binary, the same inputs at the same paths and the same output-deciding options (binary.resume_contract; scheduling options such as --threads no longer count, except for binaries that still record them).

json_summary.params_semantics: every argparse value as given, plus how the binary path was resolved (gpu_bin_source: argument, environment:FASTICGN_GPU_BIN, config:<file>, repository_build, legacy_lab_path or unresolved; path_resolution_notes: config-file problems and the deprecated-lab-path note, usually empty) and the effective input mode. gpu_bin is already absolute. The effective measurement lines and the rest of the geometry are in events[].geometry.
json_summary.status_semantics: ok or fail for that event, decided by severity: fail when the event could not produce its result or any of its warnings has severity fail. Read it for every event: without --strict a campaign exits 0 even when events failed, and a single event whose COD came out empty (cod_empty) still exits 0 as it always did.
json_summary.cod_csv_semantics: path of the COD CSV this run wrote, filled only when the event's status is ok; null in full-field mode and for every failed event. A file found at the target path of a failed event is reported as stale_cod_csv when this run did not write it; an empty COD (cod_empty) is still written as a header-only file, as before, and named in that warning.
json_summary.field_dir_semantics: the event's frame directory (full-field mode: the frame payloads; COD mode: _frames_<event>), as in 638ad18 whether or not it still exists; field_dir_exists says whether it does. COD mode deletes it after the aggregation, an empty COD included, unless --keep-frames (or, for an empty COD, --strict), so it usually no longer exists there; events whose binary or aggregation failed keep it. MCP results null a field_dir that does not exist (mcp.results.nulled_paths).
json_summary.cod_mode_semantics: the aggregation that actually produced cod_csv: naive (the default since 2026-10-05) or fillboundary, null in full-field mode; cod_method is the requested method and cod_mode the one used, and they are always equal in COD mode. Under fillboundary a frame CSV without the uy column fails with cod_uy_column_missing instead of silently degrading fill-boundary to naive.
json_summary.field_mode_semantics: cod when --interface-y/--line-y selected COD post-processing, full_field otherwise
json_summary.input_saturated_fraction_semantics: fraction of the whole reference frame's pixels equal to 255 at effective depth 8 (Pillow grayscale conversion; the binary's OpenCV conversion can differ by one grey level), null at other depths or without --json-summary; it grades input_8bit_max_255 in full-field mode only (COD mode grades the measurement-line bands, input_saturation)
json_summary.input_saturation_semantics: added 2026-10-04: what input_8bit_max_255 is graded on, measured on the reference frame at effective depth 8 (null at other depths, when the reference cannot be read, or without --json-summary). basis is line_bands in COD mode and frame in full-field mode; value is the graded fraction (line_bands: the largest band_fraction, null when no line has a band; frame: the whole frame) and threshold the --saturation-warn-fraction it is compared with; frame_fraction = input_saturated_fraction; severity is the level input_8bit_max_255 gets (info when value <= threshold and the file is an 8-bit container, warn above it, when value is null, or whenever container_bit_depth > 8), null when no reference pixel is 255 and the warning is not raised. lines (COD mode, one entry per measurement line in L0, L1 order; empty in full-field mode): y is the line as passed to the binary; band_rows [y - r, y + r] and band_cols ([x0 - r, x1 + r] for --roi-cols x0,x1, else the binary's first and last POI column on the line +/- r), inclusive and clipped to the image, bound the band, the pixels of the line's subsets that enter the COD aggregation; band_fraction is the fraction of those pixels at 255; subsets is the number of those subsets (POI columns inside --roi-cols); subsets_with_saturation and subsets_over_10pct are the fractions of them holding at least one pixel at 255 and more than 10 % of their (2r + 1)^2 pixels at 255. A line the binary skips (inside its margin) or an --roi-cols without a POI column gives subsets 0 and nulls. r, the lines, the step and --roi-cols are the run's effective values (events[].geometry). The dry-run reports the same object per event (outputs.dry_run.input_saturation_semantics).
json_summary.target_frames_semantics: target_frames_available: target images found after the reference; target_frames_selected: how many were run (smaller only with --max-frames)
json_summary.geometry_semantics: the geometry actually used: subset_radius = (subset_size - 1) // 2; line_ys = [L0, L1] as passed to the binary (line_source interface_y or line_y), null in full-field mode; line_separation_px = |L1 - L0|; gauge_mm = line_separation_px * cal; extrapolation_target_y = (L0 + L1) / 2 and extrapolation_px = [y0 - L0, y0 - L1] for fillboundary, null for naive (the default since 2026-10-05); roi_cols = the parsed --roi-cols; interface_y = the interface row this event's lines come from (L0 = interface_y - gauge//2), interface_y_source = interface_y (the --interface-y default) or event_interface_y (an --event-interface-y option), interface_y_overrides = the matching --event-interface-y options as given ([] for the default); all three null with --line-y or in full-field mode (added 2026-10-05)
json_summary.cod_stats_semantics: COD mode only (null otherwise, or when no aggregation ran), read from the aggregated values without recomputing them: rows = data rows written to the COD CSV; frames / frames_with_points / frames_without_points count target frames; x_points = POI columns inside --roi-cols; line_rows = rows found at y = L0 and y = L1 in all frame CSVs (any zncc), line_rows_present whether each is non-zero; all_zero = every written cod_um is 0.0000; max/min = the largest and smallest written cod_um (micrometre, 4 decimals) with their frame, column (px) and x_mm; abs_p95_um = 95th percentile of |cod_um|; naive_at_max_um / naive_at_min_um = 1000 * cal * (u_L0 - u_L1) at the same (frame, x), filled only under fillboundary and null under naive (the default since 2026-10-05), where max_um and min_um are themselves naive values (docs/quality-checks.md section 6); unreadable_frames = frame CSVs the aggregation could not parse (their columns stay empty)
json_summary.binary_stderr_log_semantics: path of the binary's complete stderr for this event, written next to the frame directory as <output-dir>/<frame directory name>.binary.log (not inside it, because the binary rejects files it did not write when it resumes a directory); the first lines record the command and the exit code. null when it could not be written
json_summary.binary_totals_semantics: the end-of-run counters the multi-frame binary prints on stderr, parsed when present (CSV runs write no manifest, so this is where whole-frame fallback counts appear); keys the binary did not print are absent, and the whole field is null when none was found
json_summary.binary_exit_code_semantics: exit code of the binary for this event, null when it never ran
json_summary.remediation_semantics: one actionable sentence for a binary failure that matched a known rejection (resume rejected, duplicate output name, untracked or ledger-less frame directory, locked directory, invalid GPU device, no POI, damaged frame, non-UTF-8 path, unreadable image, size mismatch, GPU out of memory), otherwise generic advice; null when the binary succeeded
json_summary.warning_details_semantics: every entry, the info ones included, with its code, severity (info, warn or fail as applied in this run; with --strict, codes listed under strict_severity fail) and full detail (the text after the first ':' or null), in the order found; it is the list the verdict is computed from. The warnings list next to it keeps the 638ad18 meaning: only the warn and fail entries, for codes 638ad18 already emitted in exactly its text (input_8bit_max_255: possible saturation_or_high_bit_truncation, the bare gpu_cli_failed, ...), for newer codes 'code: detail'. Top-level warning_details may also hold the --strict pre-check's warnings and notes, each with stage 'strict_precheck' and, when per event, 'event' (dry-run codes, outputs.dry_run); the warn-level ones also appear in the top-level warnings as 'code: message [event X]'.
json_summary.event_selection_semantics: campaign only, null for a single event (and absent from failure summaries): events_argument = --events as given (null: every event), patterns = its items, events_discovered = subdirectories with a recognized image, events_selected / events_excluded = how many --events keeps / leaves out, excluded_events = their names, interface_y_default = --interface-y (null with --line-y or in full-field mode), interface_y_overrides = one object per --event-interface-y option: argument, pattern, interface_y, events (the selected events it applies to). The dry-run has the same object (added 2026-10-05)
json_summary.verdict_rule: computed from warning_details: fail if any event failed or any entry has severity fail (pipeline_error); otherwise warn if any entry, top-level or per event, has severity warn; otherwise ok. info entries never change the verdict and never appear in the warnings lists, so warnings is empty under ok. The top-level lists carry binary, provenance, argument and --strict pre-check entries only, so they can be empty while the verdict is warn: always read events[].warnings (or warning_details).
json_summary.warnings_location: events[].warnings for per-event codes, top-level warnings for binary, provenance and argument codes; both exist only when --json-summary is given (the console prints warn and fail reasons either way)

warning_vocabulary.meaning: the event directory has fewer than 2 recognized images (with --json-summary a campaign reports such an event instead of skipping it)
warning_vocabulary.action: check the directory and --image-pattern

warning_vocabulary.meaning: the binary exited non-zero. The warnings list carries the bare code, as in 638ad18; the warning_details detail is 'exit=<code>' plus the binary's first 'Error:' line. The frame directory is kept, the full stderr is in binary_stderr_log and remediation says what to do
warning_vocabulary.action: follow remediation; 'resume rejected' means the output directory holds a different earlier run, so use a new --output-dir

warning_vocabulary.meaning: --cod-method fillboundary needs the 9-column frame CSV and found fewer columns
warning_vocabulary.action: use a binary that writes 9 columns, or drop --cod-method fillboundary (the default naive needs no uy column)

warning_vocabulary.meaning: COD mode found no frame CSV to aggregate
warning_vocabulary.action: inspect the frame directory and the binary output

warning_vocabulary.meaning: the COD CSV has a header and no data row (a line outside the image or inside the binary margin, a reversed --roi-cols, or no point valid on both lines); the header-only file is still written; the frame CSVs are deleted as after any aggregation (kept with --keep-frames or --strict)
warning_vocabulary.action: run --dry-run with the same arguments; check --interface-y/--gauge/--line-y/--roi-cols against the image

warning_vocabulary.meaning: a measurement line has no row in any frame CSV; the binary skipped it (see binary_warning)
warning_vocabulary.action: move the line out of the binary margin (subset radius + 2 px from the image edge)

warning_vocabulary.meaning: an unexpected exception inside the event (recorded only with --json-summary; without it the exception aborts the run)
warning_vocabulary.action: read the message; report it with the full command

warning_vocabulary.meaning: every written cod_um is 0.0000: both lines on one row (--gauge 0 or 1, equal --line-y values), --cal 0, or no motion at 4-decimal precision
warning_vocabulary.action: check the line geometry in events[].geometry

warning_vocabulary.meaning: some target frames have no COD point at all
warning_vocabulary.action: inspect those frames (valid_ratio, binary_totals, the binary stderr log)

warning_vocabulary.meaning: a 'Warning:' line the binary printed on a successful run (for example a measurement line skipped for being too close to the edge); at most five, then a count
warning_vocabulary.action: read the warning; the full stderr is in binary_stderr_log

warning_vocabulary.meaning: the event failed and a COD CSV at its target path was not written by this run; events[].cod_csv is null
warning_vocabulary.action: do not use that file as this run's result; use a new --output-dir

warning_vocabulary.meaning: the run replaced a COD CSV that existed before it started (for example two single-event runs into one --output-dir both write cod_result.csv)
warning_vocabulary.action: use a new --output-dir per run; earlier summaries may now name a file with different content

warning_vocabulary.meaning: two or more target images share a frame number, so the binary rejects the duplicate output names (the event fails with gpu_cli_failed)
warning_vocabulary.action: check --image-pattern and remove duplicate files such as macOS '._*' copies

warning_vocabulary.meaning: more than one image carries the reference frame number; the first in name order is the reference and the others are not used (the run itself succeeds, also under --strict)
warning_vocabulary.action: make sure the intended image is the reference; check --image-pattern and files such as macOS '._*' copies

warning_vocabulary.meaning: pooled finite zncc >= 0 fraction below 0.95
warning_vocabulary.action: look for low texture, out-of-range bands, large motion or frame fallback

warning_vocabulary.meaning: median zncc of the valid rows below 0.9
warning_vocabulary.action: check image quality, subset size and decorrelation

warning_vocabulary.meaning: no frame rows were found or parsed, so valid_ratio is null
warning_vocabulary.action: inspect the frame files

warning_vocabulary.meaning: no valid row, so zncc_median is null
warning_vocabulary.action: treat the event as unmeasured

warning_vocabulary.meaning: the reference frame, read at effective depth 8, has at least one pixel equal to 255. As a warning its text in the warnings list is the 638ad18 one, 'input_8bit_max_255: possible saturation_or_high_bit_truncation'; the graded fraction, the threshold, the whole-frame fraction and (COD mode) each measurement line's band, band fraction and saturated-subset fractions are in the warning_details detail, and as fields in events[].input_saturation. The graded fraction is, in COD mode, the largest fraction of pixels at 255 among the measurement-line bands (the pixels of each line's subsets that enter the COD aggregation) and, in full-field mode, that of the whole frame (input_saturated_fraction). info when it is at most --saturation-warn-fraction (default 0.05) and the file is an 8-bit container; warn above it, when it is unknown (no line has a band), or when the container is deeper than 8 bits (possible high-bit truncation of a 16-bit file read as 8-bit). The dry-run forecasts the level (events[].input_saturation.severity). A heuristic, not proof
warning_vocabulary.action: for warn: read events[].input_saturation (which line, how many of its subsets are saturated), look at those bands in the reference image (docs/quality-checks.md section 5) and check the source bit depth with --dry-run

warning_vocabulary.meaning: some frame files could not be parsed and were left out of the statistics
warning_vocabulary.action: inspect those files

warning_vocabulary.meaning: the frame directory already held frame files and the binary did not report verifying them (an older binary without the ledger, or a reused directory)
warning_vocabulary.action: use a new --output-dir

warning_vocabulary.meaning: in a campaign, this event's frame count differs from the unique most common count
warning_vocabulary.action: check for missing or extra images

warning_vocabulary.meaning: the binary's 'Reference input:' line was not found, so input_reference is null
warning_vocabulary.action: check the binary version and log

warning_vocabulary.meaning: the frame directory held frames of a matching earlier run and the binary verified them against its ledger ('Verified complete run' or 'Resume: N verified files') instead of recomputing or mixing them
warning_vocabulary.action: none

warning_vocabulary.meaning: --max-frames limited the run to the first N of the available target frames
warning_vocabulary.action: none; rerun without it for the whole sequence

warning_vocabulary.meaning: binary_totals.frames_with_fallback_fftcc > 0: some frames needed the whole-frame FFTCC fallback
warning_vocabulary.action: treat valid POIs with zncc < 0.8 in those frames as suspect (docs/quality-checks.md section 7); the binary stderr log names the frames

warning_vocabulary.meaning: the <frame directory>.binary.log file could not be opened; the binary's stderr was kept in memory only (binary_stderr_log is null) and parsed as usual
warning_vocabulary.action: check that the output directory is writable

warning_vocabulary.meaning: normal execution stopped before running any event (binary not found, --cal missing in COD mode, an unparsable --roi-cols, --line-y or --image-pattern, a missing input directory, no event found, an output directory that cannot be created, --strict validation failed with one entry per error, or the summary itself could not be written: summary_write_failed); events is empty and events_failed is 1
warning_vocabulary.action: fix the reported problem; run --dry-run with the same arguments first

warning_vocabulary.meaning: without --strict, an argument the dry-run rejects but normal execution has always accepted; detail starts with the dry-run error code (for example invalid_subset_size, invalid_cal, invalid_gauge, line_y_not_distinct, roi_cols_out_of_bounds, invalid_conv_threshold, invalid_gpu_device, invalid_input_alignment, invalid_step) and says what the run did instead
warning_vocabulary.action: fix the argument; --strict refuses such runs with exit 2

warning_vocabulary.meaning: the binary came from the environment, a config file, another FASTICGN_HOME or the deprecated lab path, not from --gpu-bin or this checkout's build/ trees (normal for a lab deployment configured through the config file)
warning_vocabulary.action: pass --gpu-bin when a specific build must be used

warning_vocabulary.meaning: running the binary with --version failed, so provenance is missing
warning_vocabulary.action: check the resolved binary path

warning_vocabulary.meaning: --version printed no git_hash
warning_vocabulary.action: provenance cannot be proven; rebuild from a git checkout

warning_vocabulary.meaning: --version printed no build_date
warning_vocabulary.action: provenance cannot be proven

json_summary.warning_vocabulary_note: codes are the stable prefixes of the warning strings (text after the first ':' is detail); every code the pipeline emits is listed here (a unit test enforces it). severity is the level in normal runs, strict_severity the level under --strict where it differs. The verdict depends on severity only (verdict_rule). info codes appear only in warning_details, never in the warnings lists.
json_summary.frames_semantics: number of target/output frames; the fixed reference frame is excluded
json_summary.valid_ratio_semantics: pooled finite(zncc) && zncc>=0 rows divided by all rows in successfully parsed frame CSV files; an unreadable entire frame is excluded and reported via warning

dry_run.event_semantics: target_frames is what the run will compute (after --max-frames), target_frames_available what was found, target_frame_range the first and last planned frame numbers. binary_command is the exact argv of the real run (relative binary paths are already absolute). binary_stderr_log is where the real run will keep the binary's stderr. geometry is the event's geometry as the summary's events[].geometry will give it (per-event lines and interface_y with --event-interface-y); resolved_params.geometry is the run-wide default. With --events only the selected events are listed; input.events_with_images counts every event found, event_selection the selected ones.
dry_run.input_saturation_semantics: the object the run's summary will carry as events[].input_saturation (outputs.json_summary.input_saturation_semantics), computed from the same reference image with the same code and the same effective geometry and --saturation-warn-fraction; severity forecasts the level of input_8bit_max_255 (null: no pixel at 255, no warning). null when the reference will not be read at effective depth 8: --input-depth 12 or 16, or auto with a container deeper than 8 bits (auto reads an 8-bit file as 8-bit), or when the first frame cannot be probed. It is not a dry-run warning: the plan's warnings and notes do not change.
dry_run.output_state_semantics: the --output-dir as it is now: writable means the existing directory is writable, or, when it does not exist yet, that its nearest existing ancestor is a writable directory so it can be created
dry_run.event_output_state_semantics: binary_expectation, from file names only: fresh (no frame directory, an empty one, or only a tar_list.txt left by a failed run), resume_if_unchanged (a ledger contract exists and the planned targets start with its target list: the binary resumes or verifies it when binary, inputs and parameters are unchanged, and rejects the run otherwise), reject_targets_changed (the planned targets do not start with the ledger's list, for example --max-frames shortened it; ledger_targets is the recorded count), reject_untracked (entries without a ledger, which the binary rejects), fail_not_a_directory (a file occupies the frame directory path)
dry_run.issue_semantics: event is present for per-event issues; severity is present on warnings and notes. errors are always blocking; warnings (severity warn) need a look before running; notes (severity info) are context only. As in 638ad18, a deployment configured through the config file (no --gpu-bin) gets an empty warnings list: gpu_bin_outside_checkout, line_y_overrides_interface_y, max_frames_applied and json_summary_ignored are notes. The minimal variants (argument_parse_error, dry_run_exception) have every required_top_level_fields entry too, with empty warnings, notes and events.
dry_run.error_code_notes: gpu_bin_legacy_lab_path and input_depth_truncates_container occur only with --strict (the second when the first frame's container is deeper than 8 bits and the effective --input-depth is 8; its message gives the probe's recommendation). line_y_not_distinct and the ordering/negativity part of roi_cols_out_of_bounds are checked once without reading images and therefore carry no event; the image-width part of roi_cols_out_of_bounds and the line bounds are per event. duplicate_frame_number covers duplicate target numbers only (the binary rejects the output names); a duplicate of the reference number is the warning duplicate_reference_frame_number, because that run succeeds. frame_dir_targets_changed: an existing ledger records a target list the planned one does not start with. The --events / --event-interface-y codes (invalid_events through event_interface_y_conflict) carry no event except event_interface_y_conflict; normal execution refuses them with exit 2 in every mode, unlike the other argument checks.

warning_code_semantics.json_summary_ignored: info: --json-summary was given; dry-run writes its JSON to stdout instead
warning_code_semantics.event_without_images: warn: a campaign subdirectory has no recognized image and will be skipped
warning_code_semantics.input_mode_differs_from_probe: warn: the requested input depth/alignment differs from the first-frame probe's input_recommendation; the plan stays valid and the real run would use the requested mode (for a 16-bit source read as 8-bit, silently)
warning_code_semantics.path_resolution: warn: a note from binary path resolution, such as the deprecated lab path or an unreadable config file
warning_code_semantics.gpu_bin_outside_checkout: info: the binary does not come from --gpu-bin or this checkout's build/ trees (see the --gpu-bin parameter)
warning_code_semantics.line_y_overrides_interface_y: info: --line-y and --interface-y were both given; --line-y wins and the fill-boundary target is its midpoint
warning_code_semantics.max_frames_applied: info: --max-frames plans fewer target frames than were found
warning_code_semantics.cod_csv_exists: warn: the event's COD CSV already exists and the run would replace it
warning_code_semantics.frame_dir_has_ledger: warn: the frame directory holds an earlier run's ledger; the binary resumes it only when binary, inputs, parameters and target prefix are unchanged and rejects the run otherwise (fingerprints are not compared here)
warning_code_semantics.duplicate_reference_frame_number: warn: more than one image carries the reference frame number; the first in name order is the reference and the others are not used (the run succeeds, also under --strict)

dry_run.not_checked: --dry-run does not run the binary or check that --gpu-device exists, and it does not compare the binary or input fingerprints of an existing ledger (only its target list), so a plan can still be valid while the real run is rejected (resume rejected, invalid device ordinal)
dry_run.estimate_semantics: runtime_s = start-up + frame rows x a per-row cost for the mode (cod, full_field_csv or full_field_raw; frame rows = target frames x POIs per frame), measured end to end (pipeline start-up, binary, frame parsing, aggregation and, when --json-summary is given, the summary statistics) on the date and binary in calibration; runtime_s_range multiplies it by calibration.range_factors to cover a cold page cache or a busy host. Use the upper end of runtime_s_range, not runtime_s, when you set a timeout. Byte estimates use the measured bytes per frame row of the frame format and per COD row.
dry_run.side_effect_contract: No output directory, tar-list, summary file, or GPU process is created by the pipeline. stdout is the JSON result.

mcp.server_version: serverInfo.version is the package version from pyproject.toml (1.2.0 on 2026-10-19), not the FastMCP version
mcp.interface_revision_note: revision 3 (2026-10-19): dic_describe() without arguments stopped carrying the whole mcp section and exit_codes: it returns the before-run keys of the mcp section and lists the others, which are read with section='mcp.<key>' (results.envelope names every key that left the default reply); the job model: the control key wait (false returns a job handle instead of blocking), progress in the job record and a ninth tool, dic_job_cancel (jobs; blocking calls and their replies are unchanged); and cod_um is described as the slip across the interface, not an opening. Later on 2026-10-19, without a revision change, the lab-only pitfalls moved out of pitfalls into the new top-level section lab_notes (highspeed2 bit depth, the 30 kN line conventions, parameter regimes, spaced paths in old binaries, campaign event counts): dic_get_pitfalls and section='pitfalls' keep the six general entries, dic_describe(section='lab_notes') returns the five lab entries, and the default dic_describe() reply only lists that section. revision 2 (2026-10-03): typed params schema, server instructions, tool titles and annotations, structured error fields, job runner with job record, bounded manifest queries, stricter aggregation output rules; with the batch-2 pipeline also max_frames, plans and runs in the pipeline's --strict mode, a brief built from the summary's geometry, cod_stats and warning severities, and dic_describe answering with an index by default; after review 2026-10-04 also compact replies for plans and campaigns of more than 10 events within a hard size cap, a hard max_bytes for dic_query_manifest, failed events named in the brief and in condensed lists, adoption of a job whose runner was killed, rejection of output_dir inside another run, and structured errors for names that are not UTF-8. On 2026-10-05, without a revision change, the default of the run parameter cod_method and of dic_aggregate_cod's method went from fillboundary to naive (fillboundary stays selectable; a five-column frame CSV now aggregates under the default) and run_params.campaign_keys were added. Revision 1 was the 2026-07-10 server with an untyped params object. Plans report it as mcp.interface_revision.
mcp.instructions: sent at initialize (SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS in mcp_server.py), at most 3000 characters, in this order: what COD mode measures; the workflow dic_probe_images -> dic_plan -> run tool (max_frames for a trial) -> check ok, verdict, events[].warning_details and mcp.brief (--strict, so a failed event means ok false); long jobs (wait=false, polling the job record, dic_job_cancel, never cancel a job you did not start); then traps (subset SIZE, cal mm/px, line_y order, naive COD, 12-bit TIFFs, zncc < 0, output_dir reuse, gpu_busy) and campaign keys; errors and isError; compact replies above 10 events; dic_describe gives the before-run part and section='mcp.<key>' the rest. Everything up to and including the long-jobs paragraph lies within the first 1500 characters, because some clients cut a server's instructions at about 2000.
mcp.numeric_core_modified_semantics: false means the server contains no DIC numerics; it validates input, delegates to dic_pipeline.py and reuses its COD aggregation
mcp.mode_limitation: MCP runs COD mode only: dic_plan, dic_run_event and dic_run_campaign require cal and one of interface_y or line_y, so full-field runs are not available through MCP. output_format (raw), image_pattern and image_order are not accepted either, so only images whose file names end in a six-digit frame number with a jpg/jpeg/tif/tiff/png/bmp extension are found. Use the pipeline CLI for anything else. Such requests are rejected with a message that says MCP runs COD mode only (missing_parameter or unknown_params).

tools.name: dic_describe
tools.returns: without section (or section='index'): {schema_version, contract, view: 'index', full_contract_bytes, sections: [{section, bytes, summary}], included_sections: [] (no section is included whole since 2026-10-05), mcp: the before-run keys of the mcp section (implementation, dependency, dependency_file, transport, server_name, server_version, interface_revision, supported_modes, mode_limitation, tool_count, tool_names, run_params, guardrails), mcp_view: {view: 'before_run', included_keys, on_demand: [{section: 'mcp.<key>', bytes, summary}] for every other key of the mcp section, how}, more}; at most 20480 bytes. section='mcp.<key>' (any key of the mcp section, e.g. 'mcp.results', 'mcp.errors', 'mcp.job_record', 'mcp.manifest_query', 'mcp.known_issues'): {schema_version, section, mcp: {<key>: ...}}, the same JSON path as in the whole contract; the default reply and the on_demand parts together are the whole mcp section. A section name ('mcp', 'outputs', 'exit_codes', ...): {schema_version, section, <section>: ...}. section='all': interface_contract.json as one object (over 120 KB, more than many MCP clients accept in one reply)

tools.name: dic_probe_images
tools.returns: ok, image count, reference_frame, target_frames, runnable (at least 2 images), first-frame probe, input-depth recommendation and warnings; never starts the GPU

tools.name: dic_plan
tools.returns: pipeline --dry-run plan plus ok (= valid), call_id and the mcp block (run_params.plan_mcp_block); MCP warnings are appended to warnings with source 'mcp'. Keys come in the order ok, valid, exit_code, errors, warnings, notes, mcp, estimates, then the rest; with more than 10 events each event is a compact record (results.compact_events) and the reply stays within results.max_reply_bytes

tools.name: dic_run_event
tools.returns: the pipeline --json-summary object (schema_version 1, outputs.json_summary) of a completed pipeline invocation, plus ok, call_id and the mcp block (results.run_mcp_block); with wait=false the job handle instead (jobs.handle)

tools.name: dic_run_campaign
tools.returns: the pipeline --json-summary object (schema_version 1, outputs.json_summary), plus ok, call_id and the mcp block; at most 120 selected events. Keys come in the order ok, verdict, mcp (brief first), global, then the rest; with more than 10 events each event is a compact record (results.compact_events); the full summary stays in <output_dir>/summary.json; with wait=false the job handle instead (jobs.handle)

tools.name: dic_aggregate_cod
tools.returns: ok, output_path, method, frames, x_positions, rows, gauge_mm, cod_definition and warnings; ok=false with code no_cod_rows and available_line_ys when the lines are not in the data (nothing is written)

tools.name: dic_query_manifest
tools.returns: ok, run_dir, documents, document_views, available_documents, complete, errors, truncated, max_bytes, and when needed omitted, missing_fields, hint and budget_notes (manifest_query); the whole reply, call_id included, stays within max_bytes

tools.name: dic_job_cancel
