tools.returns: ok, action ('cancelled': this call stopped the job; 'none': nothing was signalled because the job had already ended or ended by itself; 'settled': no process was left and the stale record was closed), state (the record's final state), job_id, output_dir, job_record, job (state, tool, gpu_device, exit_code, ended_at, wall_s, cancel_reason, verdict, note), progress, partial (frame_files, summary_json), processes (runner_alive, job_group_alive), note, and hint after 'cancelled'; rejections job_not_found, job_id_mismatch, job_not_owned, cancel_failed (jobs.cancel_outcomes)

run_params.schema: tools/list publishes params as a typed object: every key has a type, unit, enum or range, default and a one-sentence description. Validation stays in the server, so a bad value returns a structured ok=false result, not a protocol error. Calling a plan/run tool without the params wrapper is rejected with one explicit message.
required: image_dir (dic_run_event) or photo_dir (dic_run_campaign); dic_plan takes exactly one of them
interface_y or line_y (line_y wins when both are given)
run_params.allowed_pipeline_keys_note: mirrors PIPELINE_PARAM_KEYS in mcp_server.py; test_mcp_server checks that it, control_keys and the published schema keys agree
run_params.campaign_keys: dic_plan, dic_run_campaign: events [name or glob, no comma] -> --events; event_interface_y [{pattern, interface_y}] -> --event-interface-y PATTERN=Y each; only when given. MCP checks JSON shape, the pipeline dry-run the values; name lists in event_selection keep 10 (mcp.event_selection_view)
run_params.value_types: paths are absolute strings; numbers are JSON numbers (the string '0.5641' is rejected with a hint); input_depth, input_align and input_normalize are strings (input_depth '12', not 12: an integer is rejected with that hint); line_y and roi_cols take the forms below; keep_frames and overwrite are booleans; max_frames is an integer >= 1 (pipeline --max-frames: only the first N target frames of each event; the plan's estimates and suggested timeout use the same N)
run_params.strict: server behaviour, not a parameter: dic_plan and the run tools always pass --strict to the pipeline, so the plan and its run judge the inputs alike and cod_all_zero / duplicate_frame_number count as failures. The pipeline then repeats every dry-run check before it writes anything; if that check fails (exit 2, possible only when the inputs, the binary or output_dir changed after the MCP plan check) the run tool returns plan_invalid with the pipeline's errors, output_dir and job_record. An event that failed ends the pipeline with exit 3 and the run tool still returns the summary (verdict fail, ok false, mcp.job.exit_code 3). For a campaign the check is all or nothing: one event the dry-run refuses (for example a subdirectory with a single image, or a 16-bit event that would be read as 8-bit) makes the plan invalid and the run tool returns plan_invalid without running any event; run the other events as their own campaign.
run_params.coordinates: line_y holds two distinct non-negative rows; the order is kept and sets the sign (COD = u(L0) - u(L1); a descending pair adds warning line_y_descending). roi_cols needs 0 <= x_min <= x_max; interface_y >= 0. There is no negative or -1 'full range' shorthand. interface_y and gauge are ignored when line_y is given (warning interface_y_ignored / gauge_ignored).
run_params.gpu_device: integer >= 0 and below the number of CUDA devices the server sees (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, else /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus); when that number is unknown the plan warns gpu_device_unverified
run_params.wait: control key, boolean, default true: the run tool blocks until the job ends and returns the summary, as before. false: the tool returns as soon as the job has started, with the job handle (job_id, output_dir, job_record, summary_json, cancel_token, mcp.poll, mcp.cancel) instead of the summary; the job is then watched with dic_query_manifest(run_dir=output_dir, documents=['.mcp-job.json']) and stopped with dic_job_cancel. Every refusal that happens before the job starts (plan_invalid, gpu_busy, output_exists and the rest) comes back as for a blocking call. dic_plan accepts and ignores it. Details: dic_describe(section='mcp.jobs')
run_params.timeout_hint: dic_plan reports mcp.suggested_timeout_s = 60 s + 0.04 s per target frame, capped at 3600 (a heuristic from the lab host, where 800-frame 8-bit events took 5-26 s end to end); estimates.runtime_s is GPU-only and optimistic
run_params.overwrite_semantics: false rejects every existing output. true permits an existing empty run directory, but non-empty run directories remain rejected so stale frames are never mixed or deleted. dic_aggregate_cod may atomically replace its one explicit output_path when overwrite=true, never a file inside a run directory.

results.envelope: every tool except dic_describe and dic_get_pitfalls adds ok (boolean) and call_id (the audit log id) to its result. Compared with interface revision 1 (638ad18) results gained fields, and these default results changed shape: dic_describe() without arguments returns an index of the sections plus the before-run part of the mcp section instead of the whole contract (section='all' returns the whole contract as before). Since revision 3 (2026-10-19) that default reply no longer holds exit_codes (section='exit_codes') nor these keys of the mcp section, each read with section='mcp.<key>' or all at once with section='mcp': interface_revision_note, instructions, numeric_core_modified, numeric_core_modified_semantics, tools, results, errors, job_record, manifest_query, aggregation, known_issues, error_semantics, dry_run_side_effect_note, client_config; included_sections is now an empty list and mcp_view lists what was left out; dic_query_manifest condenses documents that do not fit max_bytes, so an array such as documents.<doc>.frames can come back as a {_condensed_list: ...} object (detail='full' and fields select the original values); plan and campaign replies with more than 10 events carry one compact record per event (results.compact_events); events[].field_dir is null in the MCP result when the frame directory no longer exists (keep_frames=false; listed in mcp.nulled_paths), while summary.json keeps the path with field_dir_exists false; dic_aggregate_cod rejects strings for numbers and booleans (cal='0.5641', overwrite='true') instead of converting them; and runs use --strict, so cod_all_zero fails its event. A run tool called with wait=false (2026-10-05) returns the job handle (jobs.handle) instead of the summary; without wait, or with wait=true, the reply is what it was.
results.ok_semantics: dic_plan: ok = valid. Run tools: ok = verdict ok or warn, the pipeline exited 0 and every ok event's COD CSV exists with at least one data row (otherwise warning cod_csv_empty); after a killed job runner the exit code is unknown and mcp.warnings has job_runner_lost. Runs use --strict (run_params.strict): exit 3 = an event failed, returned as the summary with ok false; exit 2 = the pipeline's own check refused, returned as plan_invalid. dic_aggregate_cod: ok = COD rows were written. dic_query_manifest: ok = no document failed to load. dic_probe_images: ok = the directory was probed; see runnable.
run_mcp_block: brief (one line: verdict, events ok, top-level warnings, and per event (first 3) status, frames, valid_ratio, zncc_median, the measurement rows used, COD rows and peak value, warnings as code(severity); with campaign keys the lines per event group)
stdout_tail, stderr_tail, error_lines, hint (only when the run failed)
results.nulled_paths: events[].cod_csv and events[].field_dir values that do not exist on disk are set to null in the MCP result (summary.json on disk keeps the pipeline's value, and field_dir_exists says the same) and listed in mcp.nulled_paths with the reason; with keep_frames=false the frame directory is always gone. Above 10 events the entries are grouped by field and reason (results.compact_events)
results.cod_definition: L0_y, L1_y, formula (cod_um = (u_L0 - u_L1) * cal * 1000 for naive, the default since 2026-10-05; with cod_method fillboundary each u is first extrapolated to the midpoint row), line_order and sign_convention_note (cod_um is the slip across the interface, the relative displacement of its two sides, L0 side minus L1 side, not an opening; positive when u_L0 > u_L1, so the order of the lines alone sets the sign); per_event_lines with event_interface_y
results.is_error: structured rejections are normal results (isError=false). Only MCP-level schema failures and a missing params wrapper come back as isError=true tool errors (and, defensively, a SystemExit raised outside a tool's own handler).
results.ordering: plan replies start with ok, valid, exit_code, errors, warnings, notes, mcp, estimates; run replies with ok, verdict, mcp (brief first), global, so a client that reads or truncates from the top sees the verdict first
results.compact_events: with more than 10 events (plans and campaign runs) each event is one record: runs {name, status, frames, valid_ratio, zncc_median, cod_rows, cod_peak_um, warnings (warn/fail codes as code(severity))}, plans {name, images, reference_frame, target_frames, target_frames_available, width, height, container_bit_depth, binary_expectation, errors, warnings (codes)}, with campaign keys plus line_ys, interface_y*. mcp.events_view says so: view, events, threshold, failed (runs: names of the failed events) or with_errors (plans), for runs failure_reasons ([{reason, count, events}]: each failed event's first fail-level warning as one 'code: detail' line, identical lines merged), full_summary and how_to_read (dic_query_manifest(run_dir=output_dir, documents=['summary.json'], fields=['events[3]']) for one event in full; for plans dic_plan on one event). In this view mcp.nulled_paths has one entry per field and reason ({field, reason, count, events (first 10), more_events, example_path}). Up to 10 events the reply keeps every field
results.max_reply_bytes: every reply of dic_plan, dic_run_event and dic_run_campaign stays within 49152 bytes of compact JSON, call_id and the omitted notes included: plans and run results, and also their rejections (plan_invalid from the plan check or from the pipeline's own --strict check, timeout, pipeline_failed, job_lost and the rest). Small replies are unchanged. Run results leave out, in this order, the stdout/stderr tails, params, list tails, events (failed ones kept first) and then all but ok, verdict, global and the essential mcp fields (brief, job, events_view with the failed events, their reasons and how_to_read, error_lines, hint); plans leave out known_limitations, list tails, events (those with errors kept first) and error tails; rejections leave out the tails, then the tails of errors, warnings and error_lines (for plan_invalid error stays the JSON text of the errors kept), then long strings. Each step is a note in mcp.omitted (plans, runs) or the top-level omitted (rejections): the field, how many were kept and the total, and where or how to read it in full

optional_fields: got (bounded echo of the rejected value)
errors and warnings (plan_invalid; error still holds the errors as a JSON string; when the pipeline's own --strict check refused a run, also output_dir and job_record)
omitted (a reply of dic_plan or a run tool cut to results.max_reply_bytes: field, kept_each and total, how_to_read or where)
job: state, tool, gpu_device, created_at, deadline_at (job_not_owned)
output_dir, job_record, stdout_tail, stderr_tail, error_lines (job_lost: the job runner was killed and the pipeline ended without a summary)
errors.retryable: true only for gpu_busy, output_busy (wait, or another gpu_device), timeout, job_cancelled and job_lost (with a NEW output_dir), and cancel_failed (call dic_job_cancel again)

guardrails.read_allowlist: resolved once at server start: $FASTICGN_READ_ALLOWLIST (os.pathsep-separated), else the optional config file [paths].read_allowlist, else the [/data, /media] default. A configured value replaces the default wholesale; the repository root and the MCP job root are always readable.
guardrails.read_allowlist_legacy_extra: a historical deployment convention also keeps <operator home>/DIC* readable, and only while that home directory really exists; it adds to the allowlist and never replaces it.
guardrails.job_root: resolved once at server start: $FASTICGN_JOB_ROOT, else the optional config file [paths].job_root, else ~/dic_jobs. <job_root> below means this directory.
guardrails.job_root_permissions: the job root and <job_root>/.mcp-control are created with mode 0700; existing directories keep their mode
guardrails.nested_outputs: a run's output_dir must not lie inside another run directory (one holding summary.json or .mcp-job.json) or inside any _frames_* directory: nested_output_dir. Output locks are per exact path, so a nested run could otherwise put a foreign entry into a running run's frames directory
guardrails.symlink_policy: all user paths are resolved before allowlist checks; source event-directory and recognized image/frame descendants are validated and symlink descendants are rejected; <job_root> itself must not be a symlink
guardrails.path_character_policy: C0 control characters U+0000..U+001F and DEL U+007F are rejected in user paths, in every name directly under photo_dir (stray files included, as in 638ad18) and in recognized images and frame CSVs, so tar-list records cannot be injected; names that are not valid UTF-8 are rejected where they are read, so every reply can be serialised: photo_dir subdirectories (every one is an event the plan lists), recognized images and frame CSVs (unsafe_path_characters, the name shown with \xNN escapes). A stray file under photo_dir whose name is not UTF-8 (for example a GBK-named notes file) is accepted, as in 638ad18

parameter_bounds.gpu_device: integer >= 0 and below the visible CUDA device count when it is known

guardrails.gpu_binary: resolved once at server start from $FASTICGN_GPU_BIN, the optional config file, the repository build/ trees, then the deprecated lab path; fixed for the session and agents cannot override it.
guardrails.gpu_lock: non-blocking per-device thread+file lock (flock) under <job_root>/.mcp-control. The job runner inherits the lock descriptor, so the lock lives exactly as long as the job, also after the MCP server exits; a concurrent MCP run returns gpu_busy with the holder (output_dir, start time, whether its server is still alive). A device held for a job whose record is already final is waited for in place, up to 1 s, before gpu_busy is returned: the lock is released some tens of milliseconds after the record says exited.
guardrails.output_lock: non-blocking canonical-output thread+file lock held from the state re-check through execution and the summary read, and inherited by the job runner like the GPU lock; dic_aggregate_cod takes the lock of the run directory it reads from or writes into
guardrails.lock_scope: the locks only coordinate MCP jobs of servers that share one job root (they live in <job_root>/.mcp-control): a pipeline or binary started directly on the same GPU, or a server with another job root (for example another user's ~/dic_jobs), is not seen
guardrails.timeout_action: the job runner terminates the pipeline's process group (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 5 seconds) and records timed_out; the server stops the runner itself if it has not exited 20 seconds after the timeout
guardrails.audit_log: <job_root>/mcp_audit.log JSONL; each tool call records a started and a final entry with UTC time, call_id, tool, params (capped at 8 KiB: larger params become a sha256, key list and preview) and result_code, the final entry also duration_s; middleware covers MCP schema rejection before function entry. On SIGTERM/SIGHUP the server writes the final entry of every call in flight (result_code detached for a running job, server_terminated otherwise) before it exits; only SIGKILL leaves a started entry alone. A wait=false call ends with job_started; when its job ends the server, if it is still running, adds job_finished:<verdict or error code> with job_state and exit_code, and detached if it leaves first. dic_job_cancel records cancel:<action>. The value of any argument whose name contains 'token' is written as sha256:<12 hex digits>, never as given: at any depth of the arguments, and also for a call that the schema rejects before the tool runs.

jobs.summary: run tools block until the job ends by default (wait=true): unchanged. With wait=false (run_params.wait) the same job is started and the tool returns its handle at once; the job is watched through its job record and stopped with dic_job_cancel. Still one MCP job per GPU: a second job on a busy device is gpu_busy, whichever way the first was started.
jobs.handle: reply of a run tool called with wait=false: ok true, job_id (the call_id of that call), state (starting or running), output_dir, job_record, summary_json, cancel_token, call_id, and mcp {job (state, wait, tool, gpu_device, timeout_s, deadline_at), poll {tool, arguments, poll_after_s, read}, result {tool, arguments, when, read}, cancel {tool, arguments, note}, cod_definition, warnings (MCP warnings)}. The output_dir is the handle of a job; job_id names it in the audit log.
jobs.poll: dic_query_manifest(run_dir=output_dir, documents=['.mcp-job.json'], fields=['state', 'progress']): the call a wait=false reply gives in mcp.poll, with poll_after_s (5 s for one event, up to 30 s for a long campaign: a thirtieth of the plan's suggested timeout). The record holds both fields from the start, so such a poll is complete and takes about 0.7 KB; without fields the whole record comes back (about 3 KB). state starting or running: the job is going, and the runner rewrites progress every 3 s (progress_interval_s), also when nothing changed. Final states: exited (the whole record then has exit_code: 0 = every event ok, because runs are --strict, 3 = an event failed; and verdict, events_ok and events_failed copied from summary.json), timed_out, cancelled, spawn_failed, runner_lost, job_lost. The result of an exited job is summary.json, read with dic_query_manifest(run_dir=output_dir, documents=['summary.json']): the object a blocking call returns, without its ok, call_id and mcp additions (no brief, no compact events; the size limit is dic_query_manifest's max_bytes). The GPU lock of an exited job is released within about 0.1 s of the record being written; a run tool waits for it in place (guardrails.gpu_lock), so the next job can be submitted the moment the record says exited.
jobs.progress: job_record.progress = {updated_at (UTC), elapsed_s, events_total, events_done, frames_total, frames_done, current_event, current_event_frames_done, current_event_frames_total}. The runner counts it from the files the pipeline leaves in output_dir, in plan order: an event has started once its frame directory, COD CSV or binary log exists, and is done once its COD CSV exists, a later event has started or the pipeline has ended. frames_done = the target frames of the finished events (for one that left no COD CSV: the frame files seen) plus the frame_<n>.csv files of the current event; totals come from the plan (max_frames applied). Before the runner has counted anything the record holds the plan's totals with events_done and frames_done 0. The record of a blocking run carries the same progress, so another session can watch it.
jobs.cancel: dic_job_cancel(output_dir[, job_id][, cancel_token]) sends SIGTERM to the process group of the job runner. The runner stops the pipeline's process group, which holds the binary (SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 5 s), records state cancelled with cancel_reason and exits, which releases the GPU and output locks; a blocking call that was waiting for the job returns job_cancelled. The tool waits for that, and for the job's GPU lock to be free (up to 3 s more; its note says so if it is not), and reports what happened, the final state, the partial output and whether any process is left. The runner is the one that watches the job at that moment: when it is gone (it was killed, or the one that was signalled died before it acted) the job's process group is stopped directly and the job is still recorded as cancelled, also while the server is replacing a lost runner. After 20 s the tool kills what is left itself and records cancelled. Before any signal the process is identified in /proc: its start time must be the one in the job record (runner_start_ticks, job_start_ticks) and its arguments must name the job record (runner) or output_dir (pipeline, binary) exactly, as that directory or a path inside it, so /jobs/run1 never matches a process of /jobs/run10 and a reused pid is not signalled.

cancel_outcomes.action cancelled: this call stopped the job; output_dir holds partial output and cannot be reused
cancel_outcomes.action none: nothing was signalled: the job had already ended (exited, timed_out, cancelled by an earlier call, ...) or ended by itself before the signal took effect. A cancellation repeated after the job has ended is harmless and answers none; two cancellations that arrive while the job is still being stopped both answer cancelled
cancel_outcomes.action settled: the record said starting or running, but no process of the job was left and no server was watching it: the record is closed as runner_lost (a summary exists) or job_lost. Any caller may do this
cancel_outcomes.job_not_found: output_dir does not exist or holds no .mcp-job.json
cancel_outcomes.job_id_mismatch: job_id was given and is not the id of the job in output_dir; nothing is stopped
cancel_outcomes.job_not_owned: the job is running, another MCP session started it, and cancel_token is missing or wrong; nothing is stopped
cancel_outcomes.cancel_failed: the job could not be stopped (retryable)

jobs.ownership: the MCP session (server process) that started a job cancels it with output_dir alone. Any other session needs the cancel_token of the wait=false reply: it is returned once, kept in the job record only as cancel_token_sha256, and written to the audit log only as a hash prefix (guardrails.audit_log; FastMCP's stderr warning about a call that does not match the schema is redacted in the same way). A job id is not a credential: the job record and the holder of a gpu_busy error show it. A job started with wait=true has no token, so only its own session can cancel it. The token keeps one agent from stopping another agent's job by mistake; it is not a security boundary between users of one account.
jobs.stale_records: when a job runner is killed while its job runs, the MCP server starts a second runner that watches the pipeline's process group from a session of its own (runner_lost_at, runner_replaced_at and a new runner_pid in the record): the job keeps its timeout and progress and gets a final state, runner_lost or job_lost, also when the server exits afterwards. That closes review 2026-10-04 recheck R4, where a record stayed at running for ever. A record can still stay at starting or running after its job is over when nobody is left to write it: the runner and the server were killed at the same moment, or both runners and the server were lost. The pipeline itself still ends normally and writes summary.json. Signs: progress.updated_at stops advancing, runner_lost_at and server_detached_at are both set without runner_replaced_at (server_detach_reason then says that nobody updates the record), or the time is past deadline_at. Once no process of the job is left, dic_job_cancel(output_dir) from any session settles the record (action settled); while the pipeline is still running it is an ordinary cancellation and needs ownership.

job_record.path: <output_dir>/.mcp-job.json, written by run tools before the job starts and updated by the job runner
fields: states (a sentence that explains the states, for a reader of the file)
error (spawn_failed: why the pipeline could not be started)
job_record.detached_jobs: an MCP client ends a stdio session by closing stdin, waiting about 2 s and sending SIGTERM to the server's process group. The job runner and the pipeline run in sessions of their own, so the job finishes, keeps its GPU/output locks until it ends, enforces its timeout and records its final state; the server marks server_detached_at before it exits. A later session can read the result with dic_query_manifest(output_dir). A wait=false job whose session ends is detached in the same way (the mark is also written when the session ends by closing stdin), and the session that returns can cancel it with its cancel_token.
job_record.progress: written by the job runner every progress_interval_s seconds while the job runs, and once more at the end; its fields and how they are counted: jobs.progress
job_record.process_identity: runner_pid with runner_start_ticks and job_pgid (the pipeline's pid, which leads the job's process group) with job_start_ticks name the two processes for as long as the system is up: the ticks are field 22 of /proc/<pid>/stat, the start time in clock ticks since boot. A second runner replaces runner_pid and runner_start_ticks. Records written before 2026-10-05 have no ticks and are identified by arguments alone
job_record.cancellation: cancel_requested_at and cancel_requested_by (call_id, server_pid, at) are written by dic_job_cancel before it signals; cancel_reason says who stopped the job (dic_job_cancel with its call id, or a SIGTERM to the job runner from elsewhere); settled_by marks a stale record that dic_job_cancel closed; a final state is never overwritten: the runner, the server and dic_job_cancel write one only while the record says starting or running, and a runner that finds its job already settled does not start the pipeline (or stops it)

manifest_query.candidates: *.json directly in run_dir plus */*.manifest.json, sorted summary.json, .mcp-job.json, *manifest.json, then the other names; the first 32 are listed in available_documents (truncated=true beyond), a documents filter is applied before that cut, so summary.json is always found; each document at most 10 MiB. A symlink to a path outside the read allowlist is listed with bytes null and skipped (its target's size and path are not reported); a document that cannot be decoded is an errors entry
manifest_query.max_bytes: default 16384, allowed 1024..65536; a hard limit: the whole reply (compact JSON, call_id included) stays within it. If needed the server drops top_level_keys, shortens available_documents, missing_fields and errors (budget_notes lists the steps), drops documents and finally answers with a minimal envelope. The wire carries the reply twice (text and structuredContent)
manifest_query.detail: auto (default): each document, highest priority first, in full if it still fits, otherwise in the first condensed view that fits (lists longer than 16, then 4, then 1 items summarised); compact: condensed views only; full: never condensed (a document that does not fit is omitted)
manifest_query.condensed_view: arrays longer than the threshold become {_condensed_list: {count, item_keys, numeric min/max/mean/n, boolean true/false counts, categorical counts (<= 10 distinct strings), nonempty_lists, not_ok (index, name and status of the items whose status is not ok, at most 50, so a condensed campaign summary names its failed events), first, last}}; strings longer than 512 characters are cut
manifest_query.fields: dot-separated paths with optional [index] or [start:stop] per segment, e.g. events[0].warnings or frames[100:120]; at most 32 entries of at most 256 characters; unknown paths are listed in missing_fields
manifest_query.omitted: documents that fit in no view are omitted and listed with bytes_full and, while room allows, top_level_keys; a large document no longer pushes out a smaller one of lower priority. complete is true only when nothing was condensed, omitted, missing or in errors

aggregation.line_y: rows must be present in the frame CSVs; otherwise ok=false, code no_cod_rows, the rows of the first frame (up to 50) and nothing is written. The order is kept: a descending pair adds warning line_y_descending (the sign is flipped, not corrected).
aggregation.output_path: must end in .csv; must not be named cod_result.csv or frame_*.csv; must not be inside a frames directory (a _frames_* path component or a directory holding frame_*.csv); an existing file inside a run directory (a directory with summary.json or .mcp-job.json) is never replaced, even with overwrite=true
aggregation.locks: the output lock of the run directory that frames_dir or output_path belongs to is taken (output_busy while that run is executing)
aggregation.frame_names: every frame_*.csv in frames_dir must be frame_<digits>[_suffix].csv, else invalid_frame_name
aggregation.types: cal is a JSON number; line_y and roi_cols accept the same forms as the run tools

known_issues: Run tools block by default. A job started with wait=false is polled (dic_query_manifest on the job record): there is no push notification and FastMCP tasks are not used. A client-side timeout or a closed session does not stop a job: it finishes detached, its result is read later with dic_query_manifest(output_dir), and it is stopped with dic_job_cancel (from another session only with the cancel_token).

A finished wait=false job is read from summary.json: it has no ok, mcp.brief or compact events view, which only a blocking call's reply carries. Success is job record state exited with exit_code 0 (runs are --strict), verdict ok or warn.

Progress is counted from files in output_dir (jobs.progress), not reported by the pipeline: it advances with the frame CSVs of the current event, stands still while an event is aggregated, and a failed event counts only the frames it wrote.
A cancel_token cannot be recovered: when it is lost and the session that started the job is gone, the job ends only by itself, at its timeout or by the operator's hand.

dic_job_cancel and the second job runner identify a process in /proc (start time and arguments) before they signal it; on a system without /proc they trust the pids in the job record. The server's own clean-up after a timeout (a job runner that does not answer; a job the server watches itself after both runners were lost) signals the process group in the job record without that check, as it did before the job model.

The GPU binary itself does not inherit the lock descriptors; they are held by the job runner and the pipeline process. If the pipeline process alone is killed, the job runner kills whatever is left of the job's process group (the binary) before it exits and releases the locks; only a binary started outside that process group would be missed. The other case: when the MCP server, the job runner and the pipeline process are all killed with SIGKILL at the same moment (for example pkill -9 python), nobody is left to stop the binary, it runs on, and the locks are free, so a second job can start on the same GPU. That was so before the job model as well (revision 2 at 638ad18). The job record stays at running; a caller with the job's cancel_token stops the binary with dic_job_cancel, without it (a blocking job has none) the operator must.
Lock files under <job_root>/.mcp-control are never deleted (one per GPU and per output directory used).
If the server is killed with SIGKILL the audit log keeps only the started entry of calls in flight; running jobs continue as detached jobs.
Paths are resolved before the allowlist check, so a rejected path still tells whether it exists (read_path_missing vs read_path_denied).

If the job runner itself is killed, the server starts a second runner for the job (it watches the pipeline's process group and enforces the timeout); if that cannot be started or is lost too, the server waits for the process group itself, with its locks, until it ends or reaches its timeout. Either way the exit code of that job is unknown (job state runner_lost, or job_lost when nothing is left and there is no summary). A runner and a server killed at the same moment leave the record at running: jobs.stale_records says how to recognise and settle it.

Transport-level malformed messages (JSON nested deeper than about 200 levels, integers over about 4300 digits, lone surrogates, non-JSON lines) are dropped by the MCP SDK without a JSON-RPC error and without an audit record; the call never returns. Not handled by this server (also true of revision 1).

A server process reads the contract from disk at every dic_describe call but keeps the code it started with: after an upgrade, sessions that were already open describe the new interface (for example wait and dic_job_cancel) and still run the old one, which rejects what it does not know (unknown_params, unknown tool). Reconnect open sessions after an upgrade.
mcp.error_semantics: FastMCP/Pydantic schema rejection (for example params missing entirely) is an MCP ToolError and is audited by middleware. A call that passes the public schema but fails a server guardrail returns normal structured content with ok=false/code/error/call_id and the optional fields under errors. Completed run tools return the M3 summary object with ok, call_id and mcp added, also when an event failed (pipeline --strict exit 3).
mcp.dry_run_side_effect_note: dic_plan preserves pipeline gpu_started=false and filesystem_writes=false. The MCP server separately appends the mandatory audit log, disclosed in result.mcp.

client_config.note: <python> is an interpreter with the mcp extra installed (pip install .[mcp]). The server takes no path arguments: the CUDA binary, the job root and the read allowlist come from FASTICGN_* environment variables or the optional config file (template pipeline/config.example.toml), and the plan block reports what they resolved to. ssh does not forward FASTICGN_* variables by default, so a remote server reads them from the remote config file. -T keeps ssh from allocating a terminal on the protocol stream.

pipeline.meaning: success. Without --strict a campaign exits 0 even when events failed, and a single event exits 0 when its only failure is an empty COD (cod_empty), as it always did; inspect the summary verdict, events_failed and every events[].status. With --strict, 0 means every event has status ok

post-parse preflight or runtime failure in normal execution; without --strict also a failed single event (binary failure, aggregation failure, pipeline exception) and a summary that could not be written

argument parsing failure (including a NaN or infinite --conv-threshold, a NaN or infinite --cal in COD mode, and an ambiguous abbreviation such as --d), --describe misuse, dry-run validation failure, --strict validation failure (nothing was written), or an invalid --events / --event-interface-y in any mode (nothing was written)
--strict only: the run finished but at least one event has status fail (including cod_all_zero and duplicate_frame_number, which --strict counts as failures)

binary.meaning: usage, option, input, compute, or output error

pitfalls.title: subset dual semantics
pitfalls.fact: Pipeline --subset is SIZE; binary positional subset is RADIUS.
pitfalls.action: Convert with radius=(size-1)//2. Pipeline --subset 15 means binary radius 7. Confusing them caused an approximately 100 micrometre false failure. Since 2026-09-17 the binary also accepts --subset-size 15, which is exactly radius 7 and cannot be combined with the positional radius.
pitfalls.agent_markdown: **subset 有两套语义。** Pipeline 的 `--subset 15` 是 SIZE，内部换算 `radius=(size-1)//2=7`；binary 的位置参数是 RADIUS。把 15 直接传给 binary 曾造成约 100 μm 的假失败。binary 现在也接受 `--subset-size 15`（= radius 7，输出逐字节相同），与位置参数二选一。

pitfalls.title: convergence threshold version history
pitfalls.fact: The binary's default --conv-threshold is 0.001 (builds from 2026-07-05 on); earlier builds defaulted to 0.05 and can leave an approximately 4 micrometre plateau.
pitfalls.action: Use the pipeline, which always forwards --conv-threshold 0.001, or pass it explicitly when calling an older binary directly; --help prints the default of the build at hand.
pitfalls.agent_markdown: **收敛阈值有版本史。** 2026-07-05 起的构建 CLI 默认 0.001；Pipeline 恒显式传 `--conv-threshold 0.001`。若绕过 pipeline 调用更老 binary，必须自己传 0.001；老默认 0.05 会留下约 4 μm plateau（`--help` 会打印当前构建的默认值）。

pitfalls.title: zncc<0 is a status row
pitfalls.fact: u and v on zncc<0 rows may be initial seeds, previous-frame seeds, or failed-iteration residue.
pitfalls.action: Filter finite(zncc) && zncc>=0; for displacement statistics also require finite(u,v).
pitfalls.agent_markdown: **`zncc < 0` 是状态行。** 其中的 `u,v` 可能是初值、种子或失败残留，不能当有效位移。所有统计和聚合至少过滤 `zncc >= 0`。

pitfalls.title: 12-bit data left-aligned in 16-bit files
pitfalls.fact: Some cameras store 12-bit samples shifted left by four bits in a uint16 container (the low four bits are always zero). --input-depth auto reads such files as 16-bit (it infers 12 only when the stored maximum is <= 4095), auto cannot be combined with an explicit --input-align, and the default --input-depth 8 reduces any 16-bit file to 8 bits and still exits 0.
pitfalls.action: Run the dry-run first and follow events[].input_recommendation; for left-aligned 12-bit data pass --input-depth 12 --input-align left explicitly and do not use auto.
pitfalls.agent_markdown: **12-bit 左对齐数据要显式传位深。** 有的相机把 12-bit 样本左移 4 位存进 uint16 容器（低 4 位恒零）：`--input-depth auto` 会把它当 16-bit（只有存储最大值 ≤ 4095 才推断成 12），`auto` 不得与显式 `--input-align` 同用，而默认的 `--input-depth 8` 会把任何 16-bit 文件降成 8 bit 且照样 exit 0。先跑 dry-run、按 `events[].input_recommendation` 传参；左对齐 12-bit 数据显式传 `--input-depth 12 --input-align left`，不要用 `auto`。

pitfalls.title: COD default method is naive again
pitfalls.fact: Default COD method, history: naive (u_L0 - u_L1) until 2026-07-09; fillboundary (each line's u extrapolated along its uy to the midpoint row) from 2026-07-09 to 2026-10-05; naive again since 2026-10-05, with fillboundary still available as --cod-method fillboundary (maintainer decision 2026-10-05). Why: with clean lines fillboundary is only a few percent above naive (per-frame spatial median about 5-7 percent with the default gauge 35 on two 800-frame laboratory events; 1.7-3.4 percent at the last-10-frame plateau with lines 8 px either side of the right interface row), but each line's uy noise is multiplied by the extrapolation distance: on 25 laboratory static-reference sequences the fillboundary COD noise floor is about 2.0 times naive with lines 8 px either side of the interface and about 3.5 times with lines 17.5 px either side; on the two 800-frame events the pointwise ratio (points with |naive| > 50 micrometres) spanned about 0.8 to 1.3 between the 1st and 99th percentiles, and the event maxima were 1.27 and 1.43 times the naive value at the same point. A line inside the interface transition band also biases fillboundary far more than naive: with the interface row 2 px off, four laboratory events gave fillboundary 77-79 percent of the plateau jump and naive 93-94 percent (last 10 frames). The laboratory's own line conventions per dataset are in lab_notes (cod-lab-line-conventions).
pitfalls.action: Leave --cod-method out (naive) unless fill-boundary semantics are required. A COD made between 2026-07-09 and 2026-10-05 without --cod-method is fillboundary: reproduce it with --cod-method fillboundary, and read events[].cod_mode of any summary rather than assuming. When fillboundary is used, quote the naive value at the same point next to its extremes (cod_stats.naive_at_max_um / naive_at_min_um, filled only under fillboundary) and the 95th percentile of |COD| (cod_stats.abs_p95_um), or use per-frame medians or percentiles (docs/quality-checks.md, section 6). Pass --gauge explicitly; omitting it means 35. Measure the interface row of each dataset first and keep both lines outside the transition band: neither the dry-run nor a campaign verdict of ok checks that. One campaign covers events with different interface rows with --interface-y for the default row and --event-interface-y PATTERN=ROW for the others (before 2026-10-05 a campaign took one row and was run once per group).
pitfalls.agent_markdown: **COD 默认口径的沿革：现在是 naive。** 默认口径 2026-07-09 以前是 `naive`（两测线 `u` 直接差分），2026-07-09 至 2026-10-05 是 `fillboundary`（各测线 `u` 沿 `uy` 外推到两线中点再相减），2026-10-05 起改回 `naive`，`fillboundary` 仍可用 `--cod-method fillboundary` 选（2026-10-05 拍板）。原因：测线干净时 fill-boundary 只比 naive 高几个百分点（默认 gauge 35、两个 800 帧实验室事件的逐帧空间中位数约 5–7%；界面 ±8 px、界面行给对时末 10 帧平台约 1.7–3.4%），但每条测线的 `uy` 噪声被外推距离放大：25 组实验室 static-ref 上，测线距界面 ±8 px 时 fill-boundary 噪声底约为 naive 的 2.0 倍，±17.5 px 时约 3.5 倍；那两个 800 帧事件上逐点比值（只计 naive 绝对值 > 50 μm 的点）1%–99% 分位约 0.8–1.3，事件最大值是同一点 naive 的 1.27 和 1.43 倍。测线进了界面过渡带时 fill-boundary 偏得也多得多：界面行错 2 px 的四个实验室事件，末 10 帧 fill-boundary 只有平台跳变的 77–79%，naive 为 93–94%。本实验室各数据集的测线惯例见 `lab_notes`（cod-lab-line-conventions）。做法：不需要 fill-boundary 语义就不传 `--cod-method`（即 naive）；2026-07-09 至 2026-10-05 之间没传 `--cod-method` 的结果是 fill-boundary，复现要显式 `--cod-method fillboundary`，以 summary 的 `events[].cod_mode` 为准。用 fill-boundary 时报极值要并列同一点的 naive 值（`cod_stats.naive_at_max_um`，只在 fillboundary 下有值）和 |COD| 的 p95（`cod_stats.abs_p95_um`），或用中位数/分位数（见 `docs/quality-checks.md` 第 6 节）。`--gauge` 要显式写，不写就是 35。换一批数据先量界面行，两条测线都要在过渡带外：dry-run 和 campaign 全 `ok` 都查不出这一点。界面行不同的事件可以在一次 campaign 里用 `--interface-y` 给默认行、`--event-interface-y PATTERN=行` 给其余事件（2026-10-05 起；此前一次 campaign 只能给一个界面行，要分组跑）。

pitfalls.title: v9 and earlier have five columns
pitfalls.fact: Without uy, fill-boundary is mathematically identical to naive. Since 2026-09-17 the pipeline refuses --cod-method fillboundary on such CSVs with cod_uy_column_missing instead of degrading silently. The default naive (since 2026-10-05) needs no uy column and aggregates them.
pitfalls.action: With the default naive a five-column CSV is fine and the summary records cod_mode: naive. Use a nine-column v10+ binary whenever fill-boundary semantics are required.
pitfalls.agent_markdown: **v9 及更早只有 5 列。** 缺少 `uy` 的 CSV 让 fill-boundary 数学上等同 naive；2026-09-17 起显式 `--cod-method fillboundary` 遇到这种 CSV 直接报 `cod_uy_column_missing`，不再静默降级。默认的 `naive`（2026-10-05 起）不需要 `uy`，5 列可以直接聚合（summary 记 `cod_mode: naive`）；要 fill-boundary 就用 9 列 binary（v10+）。

lab_notes.title: highspeed2 12-bit left alignment
lab_notes.fact: highspeed2 TIFF is a uint16 container carrying 12-bit data shifted left by four bits; all low four bits are zero.
lab_notes.action: Use --input-depth 12 --input-align left. Do not use auto: it infers 16, and auto plus explicit align is rejected.
lab_notes.agent_markdown: **highspeed2 是 12-bit 左移。** TIFF 容器为 uint16，但低 4 位恒零；正确参数是 `--input-depth 12 --input-align left`。`auto` 会误判成 16，而且 `auto` 不得与显式 `--input-align` 同用。对这批数据不要用 `auto`。

lab_notes.title: 30 kN line conventions and interface rows per segment
lab_notes.fact: The lab's 30 kN convention is lines 8 px either side of the interface row, registered per segment (2026-10-05, measured per event on the last 10 frames): event01-20 interface 131, --interface-y 131 --gauge 16 (lines 123/139); event21-25 interface 133, --interface-y 133 --gauge 16 (lines 125/141; event24 has no resolvable rupture and takes its segment's 133). The whole specimen moved about 2 px down in the camera frame between event20 and event21 (20 kN likewise between event26 and event27, interface about 131 then about 133). With the other segment's row one line lies inside the transition band (fillboundary: event21/22/23/25 77-79 percent with 131, 103-105 percent with 133; event10 103 percent with 131, 81 percent with 133). --interface-y 133 without --gauge gives the default 35 (lines 116/150, the geometry used before 2026-10-05). Over the other config1 loads and lowrough-20260918 the measured interface rows span 128-133.5 (docs/lab/simulacrum.md, dataset table).
lab_notes.action: Use the interface row of the event's segment; one campaign covers both segments with --interface-y 131 --event-interface-y 'event2[1-5]=133' (docs/lab/simulacrum.md; before 2026-10-05 a campaign took one row and was run once per segment). Pass --gauge 16 explicitly for the lab's 8 px convention. Leave --cod-method out (naive) for lab COD; the general rules are pitfall cod-method-generation.
lab_notes.agent_markdown: **30 kN 的测线惯例与分段界面行。** 实验室惯例是界面 ±8 px，界面行按段登记（2026-10-05 逐事件实测末 10 帧）：event01–20 界面 131，`--interface-y 131 --gauge 16`（测线 123/139）；event21–25 界面 133，`--interface-y 133 --gauge 16`（测线 125/141；event24 没有可分辨的破裂，按段取 133）。原因是整个试样在 event20 → 21 之间相对相机向下平移约 2 px（20 kN 同样在 event26 → 27 之间，界面约 131 → 约 133）。用错段的界面行会有一条测线落进过渡带（fill-boundary：event21/22/23/25 按 131 为 77–79%、按 133 为 103–105%；event10 按 131 为 103%、按 133 为 81%）。`--interface-y 133` 不带 `--gauge` 是默认 35（测线 116/150，2026-10-05 以前的几何）。其他 config1 载荷和 lowrough-20260918 实测在 128–133.5（见"数据集惯例参数"表）。一次 campaign 用 `--interface-y 131 --event-interface-y 'event2[1-5]=133'` 覆盖两段（2026-10-05 起；此前只能按段分开跑）。实验室 COD 不传 `--cod-method`（即 naive），`--gauge 16` 要显式写；通用规则见 pitfall cod-method-generation。

lab_notes.title: two parameter regimes
lab_notes.fact: GPU production uses size 15 step 1: 171024 POI on the full 1036x186 config1 frame. LabAgent/figures commonly use size 21 step 5: 6699 POI on the same full frame. The binary's full-field grid puts a POI at every x = m, m+step, ... < width - m and y = m, m+step, ... < height - m with m = radius + 2 (radius 7: 1018 x 168; radius 10, step 5: 203 x 33). LabAgent's own ROI is not recorded.
lab_notes.action: Check the regime before comparing any numerical result.
lab_notes.agent_markdown: **不要混用两套 regime。** GPU 生产常用 size 15、step 1（config1 1036×186 全幅 171,024 个 POI）；LabAgent/绘图常用 size 21、step 5（同一全幅 6,699 个 POI；LabAgent 自己的 ROI 未登记）。binary 全幅网格：x 从 m 起每 step 取一点、到 宽 − m 前止，y 同理，m = radius + 2（radius 7 为 1018 × 168，radius 10、step 5 为 203 × 33）。比较结果前先核对 regime。

lab_notes.title: paths containing spaces
lab_notes.fact: Tar-list paths containing spaces are supported from commit 9b22758 and release v1.1.0.
lab_notes.action: Use v1.1.0+; older parsers can silently split paths incorrectly.
lab_notes.agent_markdown: **带空格路径需要新 binary。** `9b22758` 起支持（随 v1.1.0 发布）；更老版本的 tar-list parser 会错切。

lab_notes.title: campaign event counts
lab_notes.fact: The config1-bimaterial data directories hold 85 events for 10/20/30 kN (30 + 30 + 25) and 32 for 40 kN (run1-run3). The old batch script batch_bimaterial_altbin.py drops 10kN/event05 and 30kN/event24 as historical bad events, which gives the historical counts 83 (10/20/30 kN) and 115 (with 40 kN); why they were dropped is not recorded. Measured 2026-10-05: in their last 10 frames neither shows a resolvable displacement jump across the interface (0.0003 and 0.0005 px between rows 111-122 and 140-151), so no interface row can be measured for them. The current pipeline drops nothing: campaigns process all 85.
lab_notes.action: Say which count you mean (85 on disk and processed by campaigns, or 83/115 after the old script's two exclusions) and give the load range.
lab_notes.agent_markdown: **事件数口径。** `config1-bimaterial` 的 10/20/30 kN 数据目录里共 85 个事件（30 + 30 + 25），40 kN 另有 32 个（run1–run3）。旧批处理脚本 `batch_bimaterial_altbin.py` 把 `10kN/event05`、`30kN/event24` 当作历史坏事件剔除，所以历史统计是 83 个（含 40 kN 为 115 个）；剔除原因没有记录；2026-10-05 实测这两个事件末 10 帧在界面两侧没有可分辨的位移跳变（行 111–122 对 140–151 只差 0.0003 / 0.0005 px），界面行无法判定。现行 pipeline 不做剔除，campaign 会处理全部 85 个。引用时写明是哪个口径和载荷范围。

known_limitations: --input-depth auto misclassifies left-shifted 12-bit values above 4095 as 16-bit.
A dark left-shifted 12-bit first frame whose stored max is <=4095 is ambiguous with right-aligned 12-bit.
Multi-frame auto inference may differ by target; summary input_reference reports only the reference frame's effective mode.
Ordinary pipeline CSV mode has no raw-format manifest; multi-frame CSV runs have .opencorr-state integrity metadata. Summary provenance is read from binary --version.

Raw-format and diagnostics manifests keep their record layouts and have carried an additive engine block since 2026-09-17. The separate .opencorr-state contract records git_hash/build_date, a binary fingerprint, input fingerprints and run parameters. Requested input options still do not claim per-frame effective auto modes.

With the default --input-depth 8 a 16-bit image is reduced to 8 bits by OpenCV before the solver sees it, and the run still exits 0. Binaries whose --version prints a version= line (built from 2026-10-05 on) probe the reference once more and print a warning that names the stored depth and the option to pass, repeated in the status line and recorded as input_image.reference_source_depth in raw manifests; the pipeline does not read that warning into its summary (it stays in events[].binary_stderr_log). Earlier binaries cannot warn. In both cases the dry-run input_mode_differs_from_probe warning and, in the summary, input_8bit_max_255 (a warn whenever the reference file's container is deeper than 8 bits) remain, and --strict refuses such a run.

The 8-bit max=255 warning (input_8bit_max_255) is a heuristic for possible saturation or high-bit truncation, not proof. It is info while the graded fraction of pixels at 255 is within --saturation-warn-fraction (default 0.05, not calibrated against correlation error) and warn above it. COD mode grades the bands of the subsets that enter the COD aggregation, on the reference frame only (later frames can saturate where the reference does not); full-field mode grades the whole reference frame, which can be dominated by bright pixels outside the region you analyse.

Dry-run probes only each event's first frame; its runtime/disk estimates are linear models calibrated on one host on one date (estimates.calibration), so use the upper end of runtime_s_range for timeouts.
The C++ binary has no --describe; the pipeline's --describe (this file) is authoritative for both.
Summary frames counts target/output frames and excludes the fixed reference frame.

Without --strict, normal execution still runs with arguments the dry-run rejects (legacy compatibility) and only reports them as argument_warning: a negative --cal flips the sign of cod_um and x_mm, an even --subset is rounded down (16 runs as 15), --gauge 0 or 1 puts both lines on the same row. It does not apply the image-aware checks either; their consequences surface after the run as cod_line_missing or cod_empty. --strict applies every dry-run check first.

Without --strict, a COD result that measured nothing keeps its historical exit code: a single event whose COD CSV is header-only still exits 0 although its status is fail (cod_empty, with cod_line_missing when the binary skipped a line) and the console says so, and an all-zero COD is only a warning (cod_all_zero). Read the summary, or use --strict, which exits 3.

When an event fails, a COD CSV left at the same path by an earlier run is neither moved nor deleted, as in 638ad18: it keeps its name (<event>.csv, cod_result.csv), so a script that only checks the exit code and then globs the CSVs reads the earlier run's result. events[].cod_csv is null and stale_cod_csv names the file. Without --strict a campaign whose events failed still exits 0, although the console no longer reports it as all done. Use a new --output-dir per run and read every events[].status.

Single-event COD mode always writes <output-dir>/cod_result.csv, so two events run into the same --output-dir still overwrite each other's COD CSV; the dry-run reports cod_csv_exists and the second run's summary cod_csv_replaced, but the first run's summary keeps naming the replaced file.
A relative --gpu-bin, FASTICGN_GPU_BIN or config gpu_bin is made absolute against the current working directory, not against the config file's location.
The binary's complete stderr is kept for every event in <output-dir>/<frame directory name>.binary.log (about 0.5 KB per frame), so a campaign of long events accumulates logs in the output root.

FFTCC initial guesses can only represent integer displacements in [-(r-1), +r] around the seed for subset radius r (correlation window 2r); in synthetic tests they were reliable only to about +/-(r-2) px. A whole-frame fallback recomputes the frame from a zero guess and merges it per POI with the seeded attempt (engine.frame_fallback_policy), so it never leaves more bad POIs than the seeded attempt, but it cannot recover motion beyond that range, and POIs neither pass recovers restart from zero on the next frame: once triggered, the fallback can fire on every later frame, each time adding a full-frame FFTCC + ICGN. Builds without frame_fallback_policy kept the from-scratch result even when it was worse, so near the subset radius a single disturbed frame could lose tracking for every later frame. Watch the raw manifest frames[].fallback_used and valid_ratio.

Each tar-list line must end with a whitespace-free output_name. With a spaced path but missing output_name, the final path segment can be silently misread as the output name; the final literal tab wins as delimiter when present.

Multi-frame output uses an integrity record in .opencorr-state. Resume requires the same binary, reference, output-deciding parameters and identical target prefix (append allowed; see binary.resume_contract for what is compared and what a rejection says), and validates file bytes/digests. Missing files are recovered by replay from frame 1 to restore temporal history; verified existing frame payloads are not rewritten. Legacy/untracked outputs are rejected; damaged tracked frames are rejected unless --repair quarantines and regenerates them. Failed pipeline runs retain intermediate frames and tar_list.txt for recovery.

--durability rename is the default and issues no fsync per frame: publication stays crash-consistent and every rejection still holds, but after a power loss or kernel panic an already published frame may be incomplete. That damage is detected by digest on the next run and repaired with --repair; --durability fsync buys power-loss durability at roughly four fsync per frame.
Non-UTF-8 reference/target/output/diagnostics paths and output names are rejected at startup because the JSON ledger and manifests must be valid UTF-8.

--strict checks a campaign as a whole before it starts: one event the dry-run refuses (for example a subdirectory with a single image, or a 16-bit event read as 8-bit) stops every event with exit 2. Without --strict the other events run. Fix or move the refused event, or run the others as their own campaign.
MCP run overwrite=true is deliberately stricter than the legacy pipeline: it accepts only an existing empty run directory and never deletes or mixes a non-empty run directory.
